title: Diamond Sūtra

atts.t: In the Tibetan language: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra called the Diamond Cutter Perfection of Wisdom.

i.sp: Diamond Cutter Perfection of Wisdom
i.ev: Tibetan order is 'ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་རྡོ་རྗེ་གཅོད་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་' (Perfection of Wisdom called Diamond Cutter), then 'ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་མདོ'. The English inverts the Tibetan title order and is inconsistent with the rendering of the same title in 0-1 ('Perfection of Wisdom called the Diamond Cutter'). Chone Drakpa Shedrub 1-2 glosses the title as the Perfection of Wisdom that is the Diamond Cutter.
i.fx: The Noble Perfection of Wisdom called the Diamond Cutter, a Mahāyāna Sūtra.

atts.t: In the Tibetan language: The Noble Perfection of Wisdom called the Diamond Cutter, a Mahāyāna sūtra.

judge.reason: Translation A reflects the Tibetan syntax more closely, where the specific title is followed by the broader class "Mahāyāna sūtra."

atts.t: Having given up later alms, he set aside his alms bowl and Dharma robe, washed his feet, sat cross-legged on the arranged seat, straightened his body, and remained, having established mindfulness to the fore.

i.sp: Having given up later alms
i.ev: 'ཟས་ཕྱི་མའི་བསོད་སྙོམས་སྤངས་ནས': Chone Drakpa Shedrub 1-6 glosses 'ཟས་ཕྱི་མ་ཕྱི་དྲོའི་བསོད་སྙོམས་ཟ་བ་སྤངས་ནས' (abandoned eating the afternoon alms food); Kamalaśīla 3-7 likewise reads it as the later (afternoon) meal/alms, which he gave up. 'Later alms' does not convey that the later (afternoon) alms meal is what is renounced.
i.fx: Having given up the alms-food of the later (afternoon) meal

atts.t: Having given up the alms of the later meal, he set aside his alms bowl and Dharma robe, washed his feet, sat cross-legged on the arranged seat, straightened his body, and remained, having established mindfulness to the fore.

judge.reason: Translation A correctly translates 'ཟས་ཕྱི་མའི་' as 'of the later meal,' whereas B translates it incorrectly as 'later alms.'

atts.t: "Blessed One, it is wonderful how the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, has benefited the bodhisattva great beings with all the supreme benefits, and how the Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva great beings with all the supreme entrustments. Blessed One, it is wonderful! Sugata, it is wonderful!"

i.sp: with all the supreme benefits ... with all the supreme entrustments
i.ev: 'ཕན་གདགས་པའི་དམ་པ་ཇི་སྙེད་པས་ཕན་གདགས་པ' and 'ཡོངས་སུ་གཏད་པའི་དམ་པ་ཇི་སྙེད་པས་ཡོངས་སུ་གཏད་པ': 'ཇི་སྙེད་པས' expresses the extent or degree (Sanskrit 'yāvad eva ... paramena anugraheṇa ... paramayā parīndanayā'; Kamalaśīla 3-10 glosses 'ཕན་གདགས་པ་གང་ཇི་སྙེད་པ་དེ་སྙེད་ཀྱིས་'), not a totality. The English adds 'all' and pluralises, implying every supreme benefit and entrustment rather than to what supreme extent the benefit and entrusting were given.
i.fx: how supremely the Tathāgata ... has benefited the bodhisattva great beings, to what supreme extent he has benefited them, and to what supreme extent the Tathāgata has entrusted them

atts.t: Blessed One, it is wonderful to what supreme extent the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, has benefited the bodhisattva great beings, and to what supreme extent the Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva great beings. Blessed One, it is wonderful! Sugata, it is wonderful!

i.sp: Blessed One, it is wonderful to what supreme extent
i.ev: The Tibetan has the ཇི་སྙེད་པས ... ནི topic clauses followed by a single exclamation བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ངོ་མཚར་ལགས་སོ, then བདེ་བར་གཤེགས་པ་ངོ་མཚར་ལགས་སོ. The English gives "Blessed One, it is wonderful" twice (once opening the sentence, once after it), i.e. one more exclamation than the Tibetan has.
i.fx: To what supreme extent the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha, has benefited the bodhisattva great beings, and to what supreme extent the Tathāgata has entrusted the bodhisattva great beings — Blessed One, it is wonderful! Sugata, it is wonderful!

judge.reason: Translation B better captures 'ཕན་གདགས་པའི་དམ་པ་' as a noun phrase ('supreme benefits') rather than an adverbial 'supreme extent.'

atts.t: Therefore, Subhūti, listen well and hold it thoroughly in mind, and

i.sp: listen well and hold it thoroughly in mind
i.ev: 'ཉོན་ལ་ལེགས་པར་རབ་ཏུ་ཡིད་ལ་ཟུངས་ཤིག' has three injunctions (Sanskrit 'śṛṇu, sādhu ca suṣṭhu ca manasi kuru'). Kamalaśīla 3-15 explains them as three separate steps against the three faults of a pot turned upside down, a dirty pot, and a leaky pot: 'ཉོན་ལ' (listen), 'ལེགས་པར' (rightly, without error) and 'རབ་ཏུ་ཡིད་ལ་ཟུང' (hold thoroughly in mind). The English merges 'ལེགས་པར' into 'listen well' and so loses the threefold structure.
i.fx: listen, attend properly, and hold it thoroughly in mind

atts.t: Therefore, Subhūti, listen, attend properly, and hold it thoroughly in mind, and

judge.reason: Translation A matches the Tibetan exactly; B adds 'attend properly', which corresponds to the Sanskrit but is absent in the Tibetan.

atts.t: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think in this way: 'However many sentient beings are subsumed by the subsumption of sentient beings—whether born from eggs, or born from a womb, or born from warmth and moisture, or miraculously born, or having form, or without form, or having perception, or neither with perception nor without perception—however many are designated by conceptual designation as sentient beings in the realm of sentient beings, all those I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the expanse of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates.'

i.sp: having perception, or neither with perception nor without perception
i.ev: The Tibetan segment itself reads འདུ་ཤེས་ཅན་ནམ། འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་མིན་ནམ and has no separate འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་པ; the English follows it. But the Sanskrit has saṃjñino vā asaṃjñino vā naivasaṃjñino nāsaṃjñino vā, and Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-7 (འདུ་ཤེས་མེད་པ་དང༌), Kamalaśīla 3-18 and Vasubandhu 2-4 all list 'without perception' as its own class, so the English drops a class the tradition counts.
i.fx: having perception, or without perception, or neither with perception nor without perception (the Tibetan lacks 'without perception'; consider restoring it with an [Ed:] note)

atts.t: Subhūti, here one who has correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle should think in this way: 'However many sentient beings are subsumed by the subsumption of sentient beings—whether born from eggs, or born from a womb, or born from warmth and moisture, or miraculously born, or having form, or without form, or having perception, or without perception, or neither with perception nor without perception—however many are designated by conceptual designation as sentient beings in the realm of sentient beings, all those I shall lead to complete nirvāṇa in the expanse of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates.'

i.sp: however many are designated by conceptual designation as sentient beings in the realm of sentient beings
i.ev: Tibetan: སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་ཁམས་ཇི་ཙམ་སེམས་ཅན་དུ་གདགས་པའི་བརྟགས་པ་དེ་དག་ཐམས་ཅད — "however much the realm of sentient beings is designated as sentient beings". The realm is the thing designated (Sanskrit yāvān kaścit sattvadhātuḥ prajñapyamānaḥ prajñapyate; Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-7: སེམས་ཅན་གྱི་ཁམས་ཅི་ཙམ་དུ་སེམས་ཅན་ཞེས་མིང་གིས་གདགས་པས་བཏགས་པ). The English turns "realm of sentient beings" into a locative container of the beings.
i.fx: however much of the realm of sentient beings is designated by conceptual designation as sentient beings, all of those

terms: neither with perception nor without perception
expanse of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates

judge.reason: Translation B faithfully follows the provided Tibetan text, which omits 'without perception' as a separate category, whereas A inserts it.

atts.t: Thus, the Tathāgata should be viewed as being without marks and signs.

i.sp: being without marks and signs
i.ev: Tibetan 'མཚན་དང་མཚན་མ་མེད་པར་བལྟའོ' parallels Skt lakṣaṇālakṣaṇatas ('by way of mark and non-mark'); Vasubandhu 2-20 quotes 'མཚན་དང་མཚན་མེད་པར་བལྟའོ'; Kamalaśīla 3-51 says one views the Tathāgata 'མཚན་གྱིས' conventionally and 'མཚན་མེད་པ' ultimately. The English distributes the negation over both 'marks' and 'signs', excluding the conventional marks that Kamalaśīla affirms (Chone 2-23 adds the qualifier 'བདེན་པར་གྲུབ་པའི', 'truly established').
i.fx: should be viewed as having marks and as being without signs

atts.t: Thus, the Tathāgata should be viewed as having marks and as being without signs.

i.sp: as having marks and as being without signs
i.ev: Tibetan: མཚན་དང་མཚན་མ་མེད་པར་བལྟའོ; Sanskrit lakṣaṇālakṣaṇatas. The English adds "having" and commits to a split reading (marks present, signs absent). Commentaries differ: Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-23 reads བདེན་པར་གྲུབ་པའི་མཚན་དང་མཚན་མ་མེད་པར — without truly established marks and signs; Kamalaśīla 3-51 reads མཚན་གྱིས་བལྟ ... མཚན་མེད་པ་ནི་དོན་དམ་པར; Vasubandhu 2-20 reads མཚན་དང་མཚན་མེད་པར. The Tibetan itself does not say "having".
i.fx: Thus, the Tathāgata should be viewed as mark and as without sign.

judge.reason: Translation A correctly translates the Tibetan 'མཚན་དང་མཚན་མ་མེད་པར་' (without marks and signs), whereas B misconstrues the negations to mimic Sanskrit.

atts.t: Subhūti, those bodhisattva great beings have not served a single Buddha.

i.sp: have not served a single Buddha
i.ev: Tibetan 'སངས་རྒྱས་གཅིག་ལ་བསྙེན་བཀུར་བྱས་པ་མ་ཡིན' means 'not (merely) one Buddha' (Skt ekabuddha-paryupāsita; Chone 2-26 'སངས་རྒྱས་གཅིག་ཙམ་ལ ... མ་ཡིན་གྱི། ... འབུམ་ཕྲག་དུ་མ་ལ'). English 'not a single Buddha' can read as 'none at all', which clashes with 6-15 (many Buddhas served).
i.fx: have not served just a single Buddha

atts.t: Subhūti, those bodhisattva great beings have not served just a single Buddha.

judge.reason: Translation A adds 'just', which is necessary in English to prevent the phrase from meaning they served zero Buddhas.

atts.t: They have not planted roots of virtue under a single Buddha, but

i.sp: under a single Buddha
i.ev: Tibetan 'སངས་རྒྱས་གཅིག་ལ་དགེ་བའི་རྩ་བ་བསྐྱེད་པ་མ་ཡིན་གྱི' means 'not only under one Buddha, but under many' (Chone 2-26 'གཅིག་ཙམ'; Kamalaśīla 3-56 'སངས་རྒྱས་འབུམ་ཕྲག་'). 'Not ... a single Buddha' can read as 'none'.
i.fx: have not planted roots of virtue under just a single Buddha, but

atts.t: They have not planted roots of virtue under just a single Buddha, but

judge.reason: Translation B includes 'just', which avoids the English idiom meaning 'zero Buddhas' and correctly conveys that they served many.

atts.t: Even if they were to engage in the perception of a selfless phenomenon, that itself would become for them a grasping at a self,

i.sp: perception of a selfless phenomenon
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཆོས་བདག་མེད་པར་འདུ་ཤེས' is parallel to 'ཆོས་སུ་འདུ་ཤེས' (perceiving as a phenomenon), i.e. perceiving as selfless / the selflessness of phenomena; Vasubandhu 2-27 glosses the pair as conceptualising 'ཆོས་བདག་མེད་པ'. Skt has adharmasaṃjñā. 'a selfless phenomenon' treats it as a kind of object, not as perceiving phenomena as selfless.
i.fx: perception of phenomena as selfless

atts.t: Even if they were to engage in the perception of phenomena as selfless, that itself would become for them a grasping at a self,

judge.reason: A correctly translates the terminative particle "par" as "as selfless", modifying the perception, rather than just as an adjective.

atts.t: Blessed One, if I were to think, 'I have obtained arhatship,' the Tathāgata, concerning me, 'The son of noble family Subhūti is the foremost of those abiding without affliction,'

i.sp: the Tathāgata, concerning me, 'The son of noble family Subhūti is the foremost of those abiding without affliction,'
i.ev: The Tibetan clause ends ...མཆོག་ཡིན་ཏེ, with its governing verb ལུང་མི་སྟོན་ལགས་སོ only in the next segment (7-31); the English leaves a quotation hanging with no predicate, and the conditional apodosis (Sanskrit na mām tathāgato vyākariṣyat) is not signalled.
i.fx: the Tathāgata, concerning me, [would not declare:] 'The son of noble family Subhūti is the foremost of those abiding without affliction,' —

atts.t: Blessed One, if I were to think, 'I have obtained arhatship,' the Tathāgata, concerning me, would not declare: 'The son of noble family Subhūti is the foremost of those abiding without affliction,' —

i.sp: would not declare
i.ev: The Tibetan of this segment ends ... ཉོན་མོངས་པ་མེད་པར་གནས་པ་རྣམས་ཀྱི་མཆོག་ཡིན་ཏེ། with no verb of declaring; the verb ལུང་མི་སྟོན་ལགས་སོ occurs only in the next segment (7-31), where the English renders it again. The English thus places the negated verb here as well, duplicating it across the two segments.
i.fx: the Tathāgata, concerning me, [would say]: "The son of noble family Subhūti is the foremost of those abiding without affliction," —

judge.reason: B provides the necessary verb to make the sentence grammatically complete in English, whereas A leaves the clause entirely without a verb.

atts.t: Because I do not abide in anything whatsoever, he does not declare "abiding without affliction."

i.sp: he does not declare
i.ev: The Tibetan གལ་ཏེ... in 7-30 sets up the conditional, and the agent of ལུང་མི་སྟོན་ is the Tathāgata (Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-50: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཀྱིས... ལུང་མི་སྟོན་ཏེ). The English pronoun 'he' has no antecedent in this segment and can be read as Subhūti or an arhat.
i.fx: the Tathāgata does not declare me 'abiding without affliction'

atts.t: Because I do not abide in anything whatsoever, the Tathāgata does not declare me 'abiding without affliction'.

judge.reason: A faithfully translates the segment without unnecessarily repeating the implied subjects and objects that were added in B.

atts.t: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'arrays of Buddha-fields, arrays of Buddha-fields,' it is because the Tathāgata has taught them as being without those arrays.

i.sp: taught them as being without those arrays
i.ev: Tibetan 'བཀོད་པ་དེ་དག་མེད་པར་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པར་གསུངས་པའི་ཕྱིར' and Sanskrit 'अव्यूहास्ते' (non-arrays): the arrays themselves are taught as non-existent/non-arrays; 'them ... without those arrays' is self-referential and does not state this.
i.fx: because the Tathāgata has taught those arrays as non-arrays (as nonexistent)

atts.t: Why is that? Subhūti, as for what is called 'arrays of Buddha-fields, arrays of Buddha-fields,' it is because the Tathāgata has taught those arrays as non-arrays.

judge.reason: A more accurately translates "med par" as "without," whereas B's "non-arrays" strays from the literal Tibetan phrasing.

atts.t: Subhūti, therefore, a bodhisattva great being should generate the mind without abiding in this way:

i.sp: without abiding in this way
i.ev: Tibetan 'འདི་ལྟར་མི་གནས་པར་སེམས་པ་བསྐྱེད་པར་བྱ་སྟེ' and Sanskrit 'एवमप्रतिष्ठितं' say one should generate the mind thus, in a non-abiding manner (introducing what follows); the English can be read as 'not abiding in this way'.
i.fx: should generate the mind in this way, without abiding:

atts.t: Subhūti, therefore, a bodhisattva great being should generate the mind in this way, without abiding:

judge.reason: A's phrasing and punctuation correctly ensures that "in this way" modifies "generate the mind," whereas B incorrectly implies "not abiding in this way."

atts.t: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, you should be convinced.

i.sp: you should be convinced
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཁྱོད་མོས་པར་བྱའོ' ; Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-58 glosses 'ཁྱོད་མོས་པ་སྟེ་འདོད་པ་བསྐྱེད་པ' (develop inclination/interest); 'convinced' implies a settled conclusion, whereas the Tibetan asks for receptive interest before 7-53 'ཁོང་དུ་ཆུད་པར་བྱའོ' (understand).
i.fx: you should take an interest (be inclined to it)

atts.t: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, you should take an interest.

judge.reason: B's "be convinced" is a much better contextual fit for "mos par bya'o" when the Buddha is declaring something to Subhūti.

atts.t: and were to give them as a gift to the Tathāgatas, arhats, and perfectly complete Buddhas, Subhūti, what do you think? Would that man or woman generate much merit on that basis?

i.sp: the Tathāgatas, arhats, and perfectly complete Buddhas
i.ev: Tibetan 'དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས་ལ' is one string of epithets for the same beings (Sanskrit 'तथागतेभ्योऽर्हद्भयः सम्यक्संबुद्धेभ्यः'); the English list with 'and' reads as three groups.
i.fx: the Tathāgatas, the arhats, the perfectly complete Buddhas (i.e. Tathāgata-arhat-perfectly complete Buddhas)

atts.t: and were to give them as a gift to the Tathāgatas, the arhats, the perfectly complete Buddhas, Subhūti, what do you think? Would that man or woman generate much merit on that basis?

judge.reason: B correctly omits "and," accurately reflecting that these terms are appositive titles for the Buddhas rather than separate groups.

atts.t: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because whatever is a particle of earth has been taught by the Tathāgata as not a particle."

i.sp: as not a particle."
i.ev: Subhūti's reply continues through 7-79 to 7-81 (དེས་ན་སའི་རྡུལ་ཞེས་བགྱིའོ། །, etc.; Skt tenocyate pṛthivīraja iti), but the English closes the quotation at the end of 7-78, so the following segments read as narration rather than Subhūti's speech.
i.fx: as not a particle,

atts.t: Why is that? Blessed One, it is because whatever is a particle of earth has been taught by the Tathāgata as not a particle,

judge.reason: A correctly uses a comma to reflect the continuing particle "ste", while B introduces a stray, unmatched closing quotation mark.

atts.t: Should the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha be seen by those thirty-two marks of a great man?

i.sp: Should the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha be seen
i.ev: Tibetan ends བལྟ་བར་བྱ་སྙམ་མམ, "do you think ... should be seen", a question to Subhūti about his thought (continuing 8-1 ཇི་སྙམ་དུ་སེམས); Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-68 paraphrases it as བལྟ་བ་སྟེ་གཟུང་བར་བྱ་སྙམ་མམ ("do you think ... to be taken as"). The English drops the སྙམ་ ("think") element.
i.fx: Do you think the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha should be seen by those thirty-two marks of a great man?

atts.t: Do you think the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha should be seen by those thirty-two marks of a great man?

judge.reason: B accurately translates the questioning particle 'སྙམ་མམ' (snyam mam) as 'Do you think', which A omits.

atts.t: The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, if some man or woman were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand of the Gaṅgā river, and if someone were to take up even just a four-line verse from this Dharma discourse and teach it properly to others, that person would generate on that basis far greater, incalculable, immeasurable merit."

i.sp: and if someone were to take up even just a four-line verse ... that person would generate on that basis far greater, incalculable, immeasurable merit
i.ev: Tibetan is a comparison: ལུས་ ... ཡོངས་སུ་གཏོང་བ་བས། ("than giving away bodies ...") གང་གིས་ ... བཟུང་སྟེ་ ... ཡང་དག་པར་བསྟན་ན། དེ་ཉིད་ ... བསོད་ནམས་ཆེས་མང་དུ ... བསྐྱེད་ ("whoever takes up ... and teaches ... generates far more merit"). Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-69: ལུས་ཀྱི་སྦྱིན་པ་ ... བཏང་བ་ལས་ཀྱང༌། ... བཟུང་ ... བསོད་ནམས་ལྷག་པར་ཆེའོ (merit greater than that of giving the body). The English makes two parallel "if" clauses, so "far greater" has no stated standard of comparison.
i.fx: Subhūti, if some man or woman were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand of the Gaṅgā river, someone who takes up even just a four-line verse from this Dharma discourse and teaches it properly to others would, on that basis, generate far greater merit than that, incalculable and immeasurable.

atts.t: The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, if some man or woman were to give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand of the Gaṅgā river, someone who takes up even just a four-line verse from this Dharma discourse and teaches it properly to others would, on that basis, generate far greater merit than that, incalculable and immeasurable."

judge.reason: B correctly captures the comparative particle 'བས' (bas) with 'than that', whereas A incorrectly renders it as 'and if'.

atts.t: Blessed One, in the future time, in the last five hundred years, those sentient beings who take up, write, hold, keep, read, and fully master this Dharma discourse will be endowed with supreme wonder.

i.sp: supreme wonder
i.ev: ངོ་མཚར་རབ་དང་ལྡན་པ is the same expression rendered "supreme marvel" in 8-11 and ངོ་མཚར་ is "marvel" in 8-9, 8-14; here it is "wonder", so one Tibetan term has two renderings across adjacent segments.
i.fx: endowed with supreme marvel

atts.t: Blessed One, in the future time, in the last five hundred years, those sentient beings who take up, write, hold, keep, read, and fully master this Dharma discourse will be endowed with supreme marvel.

judge.reason: Both 'wonder' and 'marvel' are equally valid translations for 'ངོ་མཚར' (ngo mtshar), and there are no other differences.

atts.t: Those sentient beings who, when this sūtra is being explained, are not terrified, not frightened, and do not become completely frightened, will be endowed with supreme wonder.

i.sp: supreme wonder
i.ev: ངོ་མཚར་རབ་དང་ལྡན་པ is rendered "supreme marvel" in 8-11 (and "marvel" for ངོ་མཚར in 8-9, 8-14), but "wonder" here.
i.fx: will be endowed with supreme marvel

atts.t: Those sentient beings who, when this sūtra is being explained, are not terrified, not frightened, and do not become completely frightened, will be endowed with supreme marvel.

judge.reason: Both 'marvel' and 'wonder' accurately translate 'ངོ་མཚར' (ngo mtshar). There are no other differences in fidelity or clarity.

atts.t: One should generate the mind without abiding in non-phenomena.
One should generate the mind without abiding even in non-phenomena.

judge.reason: A correctly includes 'even' to translate 'ཡང་' (yang), which B completely omits.

atts.t: Why is that? Subhūti, the Tathāgata speaks authentically, speaks truthfully, and speaks of suchness,

i.sp: speaks of suchness
i.ev: Tibetan དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་དུ་གསུང་བ (Sanskrit tathāvādī): terminative དུ་ marks the manner of speaking, not the topic. Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-86: ཆོས་རྣམས་ཀྱི་གནས་ཚུལ་ཇི་ལྟ་བ་དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་དུ་གསུང་བ་པོ (speaks as things really are); Kamalaśīla 3-144 likewise: ཇི་ལྟ་བ་བཞིན་དུ་གསུང་བས་དེ་བཞིན་ཉིད་གསུང་པ.
i.fx: speaks in accordance with suchness

atts.t: Why is that? Subhūti, the Tathāgata speaks authentically, speaks truthfully, and speaks in accordance with suchness,

judge.reason: B's 'in accordance with suchness' correctly captures the adverbial particle 'དུ་' (du), which is missed by A's 'of suchness'.

atts.t: Moreover, Subhūti, if a man or a woman were to completely give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the Gaṅgā river during the morning, and were also to completely give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the Gaṅgā river during midday and during the afternoon, compared to completely giving away bodies in this manner for many hundreds of thousands of millions of eons,

i.sp: many hundreds of thousands of millions of eons
i.ev: Tibetan བསྐལ་པ་བྱེ་བ་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་འབུམ་ཕྲག་དུ་མ has four number terms (བྱེ་བ koṭi, ཁྲག་ཁྲིག niyuta, འབུམ hundred-thousand, ཕྲག); Sanskrit kalpakoṭinayutaśatasahasrāṇi; Kamalaśīla 3-151 glosses བྱེ་བ་དེ་ཡང་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་ and འབུམ as further multipliers. The English drops ཁྲག་ཁྲིག (niyuta), though 8-72 renders it as 'myriad'.
i.fx: many hundred-thousands of myriads of millions of eons

atts.t: Moreover, Subhūti, if a man or a woman were to completely give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the Gaṅgā river during the morning, and were also to completely give away bodies as numerous as the grains of sand in the Gaṅgā river during midday and during the afternoon, compared to completely giving away bodies in this manner for many hundred-thousands of myriads of millions of eons,

judge.reason: B translates all three numbers ('bye ba', 'khrag khrig', 'bum phrag'), whereas A skips 'khrag khrig' (myriad).

atts.t: Subhūti, regarding whatever pleasing and not disappointing of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, I did, and whoever, when the last five hundred years of the latter time have come, takes up, writes, upholds, keeps, reads, and completely comprehends this sūtra—Subhūti, compared to this mass of merit, that former mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part.

i.sp: takes up, writes, upholds
i.ev: The Tibetan reads འདྲི་བ ('asks/inquires'), not འབྲི་བ ('writes'); the Sanskrit list (udgrahīṣyanti dhārayiṣyanti vācayiṣyanti paryavāpsyanti) has no writing item. Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-98 does say འབྲི་བ in its paraphrase, so 'writes' may be a defensible emendation, but the translation silently departs from the Tibetan as given.
i.fx: takes up, asks about [or: writes — noting the reading འདྲི་བ], holds

i.sp: completely comprehends
i.ev: ཀུན་ཆུབ་པར་བྱེད་པ is rendered 'master' / 'completely masters' in 8-53, 8-57 and 8-63 (Sanskrit paryavāpnuyāt); here it becomes 'completely comprehends', an unexplained inconsistency.
i.fx: completely masters

i.sp: regarding whatever pleasing and not disappointing of those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, I did, and whoever, when the last five hundred years of the latter time have come, takes up, writes, upholds, keeps, reads, and completely comprehends this sūtra—Subhūti, compared to this mass of merit, that former mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part.
i.ev: The Tibetan structure is: of (the merit of) my having pleased and not disappointed those Buddhas, and of (the merit of) the taking up etc. of this sūtra in the last five hundred years, 'this mass of merit' (བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་འདི་, the latter) is compared with 'the former mass of merit' (སྔ་མ). Kamalaśīla 3-163 states the former merit does not reach a hundredth of the latter. The English syntax leaves 'this mass of merit' without a clear referent (it reads as if the 'whoever' clause were the topic), and renders ཀུན་ཆུབ་པར་བྱེད་པ་གང་ཡིན་པ་ as a person ('whoever') rather than the act.
i.fx: Subhūti, of the merit from my having pleased, and not disappointed, those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and of the merit from whoever, when the last five hundred years of the latter time have come, takes up, holds, keeps, reads, and completely masters this sūtra: compared to this latter mass of merit, that former mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part.

atts.t: Subhūti, of the merit from my having pleased and not disappointed those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and of the merit from whoever, when the last five hundred years have come, takes up, asks about, holds, keeps, reads, and completely masters this sūtra—Subhūti, compared to this mass of merit, that former mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part.

i.sp: of the merit from my having pleased and not disappointed those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and of the merit from whoever, when the last five hundred years have come, takes up, asks about, holds, keeps, reads, and completely masters this sūtra—Subhūti, compared to this mass of merit, that former mass of merit
i.ev: The Tibetan sets two items against each other (…གང་ཡིན་པ་དང༌། …གང་ཡིན་པ་ལས། བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་འདི་ལ་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་སྔ་མས…): the former mass of merit = serving the Buddhas, 'this' mass = holding the sūtra. Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-98: 'of these two (service of Buddhas / writing etc. this sūtra), this latter mass of merit is greater, and the former does not approach even a hundredth of it' (བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་ཕྱི་མ་འདི་ཆེ་སྟེ། …སྔོན་མས་འདི་ལ་ཆ་བརྒྱར་བགོས་པའི་བརྒྱའི་ཆ…). The English adds two dangling 'of the merit from…' phrases that put both acts together, so the reader cannot tell what 'this mass of merit' and 'that former mass' refer to, and the comparison reads as if both acts are on the same side.
i.fx: Subhūti, there is the merit of my having pleased those Buddhas, the Blessed Ones, and not having wearied them, and there is the merit of whoever, when the last five hundred years have come, takes up, writes, holds, keeps, reads, and completely masters this sūtra. Subhūti, compared to this latter mass of merit, that former mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part

i.sp: asks about
i.ev: Tibetan has འདྲི་བ in this list, but the parallel list at 8-15 has འབྲི་བ 'write' and Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-98 reads མདོ་སྡེ་འདི་འབྲི་བ་སོགས་བྱེད་པ ('writes, etc.'); Skt has no 'ask'. The item is the scribal variant of 'write', and rendering it 'asks about' makes the list inconsistent with 8-15.
i.fx: writes

i.sp: not disappointed
i.ev: ཐུགས་འབྱུང་བར་མ་བྱས་པ: Chone 2-98 glosses ཐུགས་སུན་ཕྱུང་བ་མ་བྱས ('did not make [them] weary/disenchanted'); Kamalaśīla 3-162 'did not abandon the practice in between'. 'Disappointed' (a letdown of expectation) is not the sense of weariness or disenchantment.
i.fx: did not weary

atts.t: and even if they engage in a perception up to that of a person, it is because they are not to be called a bodhisattva.

i.sp: and even if they engage in a perception up to that of a person, it is because they are not to be called a bodhisattva.
i.ev: Tibetan གང་ཟག་གི་བར་དུ་འདུ་ཤེས་འཇུག་ན་ཡང༌། དེ་བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཞེས་མི་བྱ་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། — the final ཕྱིར་རོ answers 'Why is that?' of 8-86 and governs the whole sentence ('because ... even if they engage ... up to person, they are not to be called a bodhisattva'). The English 'even if ... it is because' leaves the concessive clause and the reason clause logically unconnected. Vasubandhu 2-95 glosses the pair as one reason.
i.fx: and because, even if they engage in a perception up to that of a person, they are not to be called a bodhisattva.

atts.t: and because, even if they engage in a perception up to that of a person, they are not to be called a bodhisattva.

judge.reason: B places 'because' in a natural syntactic position that governs the entire clause, making it significantly clearer and better English than A.

atts.t: It is because the present mind is also unapprehendable.

i.sp: It is because the present mind is also unapprehendable.
i.ev: Tibetan ད་ལྟར་བྱུང་བའི་སེམས་ཀྱང་དམིགས་སུ་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ། closes the three-part statement (10-1 to 10-3) with the reason particle ཕྱིར་རོ (Skt. tat-kasya hetoḥ ... nopalabhyate); the reason covers past, future and present mind together. The English fragment 'It is because the present mind...' reads as if the reason applies to the present mind alone (cf. Vasubandhu 2-114).
i.fx: This is because the present mind, too, is unapprehendable.

atts.t: This is because the present mind, too, is unapprehendable.

judge.reason: Both translations accurately and clearly render the Tibetan using the locked terms; the differences are purely stylistic.

atts.t: If someone were to completely fill this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and give it as a gift, would that son of noble family or daughter of noble family produce much merit on that basis?

i.sp: give it as a gift
i.ev: Tibetan སྦྱིན་པ་བྱིན་ན / Skt. dānaṃ dadyāt: 'give a gift'; the thing given is the seven precious substances filling the world system, not the world system itself. 'it' can be read as the world system.
i.fx: and give a gift

atts.t: If someone were to completely fill this three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system with the seven precious substances and give a gift, would that son of noble family or daughter of noble family produce much merit on that basis?

judge.reason: A is slightly more faithful by translating the phrase as "give a gift" without adding the pronoun "it", which is absent in the Tibetan.

atts.t: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?

i.sp: The Blessed One said, "Subhūti, what do you think?
i.ev: Tibetan བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ཀྱིས་བཀའ་སྩལ་པ། རབ་འབྱོར་འདི་ཇི་སྙམ་དུ་སེམས། is a self-contained segment; the English opens a quotation mark that is never closed in this or the following segments (10-24 to 10-28), leaving the quotation punctuation unbalanced.
i.fx: The Blessed One said: "Subhūti, what do you think?" (or drop the quotation marks, as in 10-17)

atts.t: The Blessed One said: Subhūti, what do you think?

judge.reason: B is better because A is missing a closing quotation mark, creating a punctuation error.

atts.t: Subhūti, if anyone were to say this: 'The Tathāgata has taught the Dharma,' Subhūti, they would slander me by grasping at what is non-existent and false.

i.sp: by grasping at what is non-existent and false
i.ev: Tibetan མེད་པ་དང་ལོག་པར་ཟིན་པས; Sanskrit asatodgṛhītena. Kamalaśīla (bo-kamalasila-tika 3-200) glosses ལོག་པར་ཟིན་པ as being wrongly seized through perverse clinging (ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཏུ་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པས་ལོག་པར་ཟིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་དེ་མེད་). The wrongness lies in the grasping, not in a 'false' object; 'non-existent and false' makes the object doubly characterised.
i.fx: by a mistaken grasping of what does not exist

atts.t: Subhūti, if anyone were to say this: 'The Tathāgata has taught the Dharma,' Subhūti, they would slander me by a mistaken grasping of what does not exist.

judge.reason: A correctly treats "ལོག་པར" (wrongly/mistakenly) as an adverb modifying "ཟིན་པས" (grasping), whereas B incorrectly treats it as parallel to "མེད་པ" (non-existent).

atts.t: Furthermore, Subhūti, compared to any son of noble family or daughter of noble family who, having brought together masses of the seven precious substances equal to however many kings of mountains, Mount Sumerus, there are in the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system, gives them as a gift, if someone were to take up even just a single four-line verse from this perfection of wisdom and teach it to others, Subhūti, that former mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part, up to not bearing comparison even as a cause.

i.sp: compared to any son of noble family or daughter of noble family who, having brought together masses of the seven precious substances equal to however many kings of mountains, Mount Sumerus, there are in the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system, gives them as a gift, if someone were to take up even just a single four-line verse from this perfection of wisdom and teach it to others, Subhūti, that former mass of merit does not approach even a hundredth part
i.ev: The Tibetan has two actors and a comparison: "སྦྱིན་པ་བྱིན་པ་བས་ ... གང་གིས་ ... ཚིག་བཞི་པའི་ཚིགས་སུ་བཅད་པ་གཅིག་ཙམ་བཟུང་ནས་གཞན་དག་ལ་ཡང་བསྟན་ན། ... བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་སྔ་མ་དེས་བརྒྱའི་ཆར་ཡང་ཉེ་བར་མི་འགྲོ་བ". Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-131 glosses it: the former gift's merit does not approach one part in a hundred of the latter. The English opens with "compared to" the giver, then states the giver's own merit falls short, and never says a hundredth part of what, so the comparison is hard to parse.
i.fx: Furthermore, Subhūti, suppose any son or daughter of noble family brought together masses of the seven precious substances equal to however many kings of mountains, Mount Sumerus, there are in the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system, and gave them as a gift; and suppose someone took up even a single four-line verse from this perfection of wisdom and taught it to others. Subhūti, that former mass of merit does not come near even a hundredth part of the latter, up to not bearing comparison even as a cause.

atts.t: Furthermore, Subhūti, suppose any son of noble family or daughter of noble family brought together masses of the seven precious substances equal to however many kings of mountains, Mount Sumerus, there are in the three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system, and gave them as a gift; and suppose someone took up even just a single four-line verse from this perfection of wisdom and taught it to others. Subhūti, that former mass of merit does not come near even a hundredth part of the latter, up to not bearing comparison even as a cause.

judge.reason: A more faithfully preserves the Tibetan comparative syntactic structure (compared to... if...) rather than splitting it into separate conditional suppositions like B.

atts.t: Those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle do not designate any phenomenon as destroyed or as an annihilation.

i.sp: do not designate any phenomenon as destroyed or as an annihilation
i.ev: Tibetan ཆོས་གང་ཡང་རྣམ་པར་བཤིག་པའམ། ཆད་པར་བཏགས་པ་མེད་དོ། pairs རྣམ་པར་བཤིག་པ (destroyed, locked 'destroyed') with ཆད་པར་བཏགས་པ (designated as annihilation); Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-143 reads 'ཆོས་གང་ཡང་རྣམ་པར་བཤིག་པའམ་ཆད་པར་བཏགས་པ་མེད་' as no phenomenon destroyed or designated as annihilation, and 11-8 (2-142) has them destroying by reasoning or designating annihilation. The English makes 'designate' govern 'destroyed', diverging from 11-8's rendering of the same pair.
i.fx: do not destroy any phenomenon or designate it as an annihilation

atts.t: Those who have correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle do not destroy any phenomenon or designate it as an annihilation.

i.sp: do not destroy any phenomenon or designate it as an annihilation
i.ev: Tibetan ཆོས་གང་ཡང་རྣམ་པར་བཤིག་པའམ། ཆད་པར་བཏགས་པ་མེད་དོ། — the verb བཏགས་པ 'designated' governs both rnam par bshig pa and chad pa; Skt vināśaḥ prajñapto nocchedaḥ ('destruction is not posited, nor annihilation'). Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-143: 'they have no designation of any phenomenon as destroyed or annihilated (རྣམ་པར་བཤིག་པའམ་ཆད་པར་བཏགས་པ་མེད)'; Vasubandhu 2-135: ཆོས་གང་ལ་ལ་ཞིག་བཤིག་པར་བཏགས་པ་མེད་པ. The English makes 'destroy' an action the bodhisattvas perform rather than a status they do not ascribe, and does not use the locked 'destroyed'.
i.fx: do not designate any phenomenon as destroyed or as annihilated

atts.t: After the Blessed One had spoken these words, the elder Subhūti, those monks, those bodhisattvas, the fourfold assembly of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, and the world with its gods, humans, demigods, and gandharvas rejoiced,

After the Blessed One had spoken thus, the elder Subhūti, those monks, those bodhisattvas, and the fourfold assembly of monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen, along with the world with its gods, humans, demigods, and gandharvas, rejoiced,

judge.reason: Both translations accurately and clearly render the list of the assembly and the world; the minor wording differences are purely stylistic.

atts.t: The noble Mahāyāna sūtra called the perfection of wisdom Diamond Cutter is complete.

i.sp: called the perfection of wisdom Diamond Cutter
i.ev: Tibetan title ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་རྡོ་རྗེ་གཅོད་པ is locked as a whole to 'The Perfection of Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond'; the translation instead strings together the component terms (perfection of wisdom + Diamond Cutter), which reads as an unpunctuated, ungrammatical title.
i.fx: called The Perfection of Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond

atts.t: The noble Mahāyāna sūtra entitled the Diamond Cutter perfection of wisdom is complete.

i.sp: The noble Mahāyāna sūtra entitled the Diamond Cutter perfection of wisdom
i.ev: Locked term ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་རྡོ་རྗེ་གཅོད་པ = 'The Perfection of Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond'; the English splits the title into parts and uses 'Diamond Cutter perfection of wisdom'. Also འཕགས་པ 'noble' qualifies the title (འཕགས་པ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ…), not 'Mahāyāna sūtra'.
i.fx: The Mahāyāna sūtra entitled The Noble Perfection of Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond is complete

atts.t: The Noble Mahāyāna Sūtra called the Diamond Cutter Perfection of Wisdom is complete.

terms: The Perfection of Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond

judge.reason: A follows the exact Tibetan word order for the title ("perfection of wisdom Diamond Cutter"), whereas B reverses it.

atts.t: 放棄了後餐的乞食，放下缽與法衣，洗淨雙足，在鋪設好的座位上結跏趺坐，挺直身體，將正念繫念在前而安坐。

i.sp: 放棄了後餐的乞食
i.ev: Tibetan ཟས་ཕྱི་མའི་བསོད་སྙོམས་སྤངས་ནས; Chone Drakpa Shedrub 1-6 glosses it as ཟས་ཕྱི་མ་ཕྱི་དྲོའི་བསོད་སྙོམས་ཟ་བ་སྤངས་ནས (giving up eating afternoon alms). '後餐' can be misread as a second/next meal rather than the post-meal (afternoon) alms the Buddha refrains from.
i.fx: 捨棄了午後（後食）的乞食

atts.t: 捨棄了午後的乞食，放下缽與法衣，洗淨雙足，在鋪設好的座位上結跏趺坐，挺直身體，將正念繫念在前而安坐。

judge.reason: A's "後餐的" translates "ཟས་ཕྱི་མའི་" (later meal) more literally and accurately than B's inferred "午後的" (afternoon).

atts.t: 世尊！如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者、佛，以何等最勝之利益，利益諸菩薩摩訶薩；如來以何等最勝之付囑，付囑諸菩薩摩訶薩。世尊，這真是稀有！善逝，這真是稀有！

i.sp: 正等覺者、佛
i.ev: Tibetan ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས is one epithet (locked: 正等覺者, with སངས་རྒྱས contained within it); the Tibetan list is only Tathāgata, arhat, perfectly complete Buddha (Sanskrit tathāgatena arhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena). The enumeration 正等覺者、佛 creates a fourth epithet.
i.fx: 正等覺佛

atts.t: 世尊、如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者，佛以所有最勝的饒益來饒益諸菩薩摩訶薩，以及如來以所有最勝的付囑來付囑諸菩薩摩訶薩，世尊！這真是稀有！善逝！這真是稀有！

i.sp: 世尊、如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者，佛以
i.ev: Tibetan བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ is the vocative; the agent (ཀྱིས) is the single phrase དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས (Skt tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena). The translation lists 世尊 and the three epithets as one string of vocatives and then introduces a separate agent 佛, duplicating སངས་རྒྱས (already inside 正等覺者) and obscuring who benefited the bodhisattvas.
i.fx: 世尊，如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者以所有最勝的饒益來饒益諸菩薩摩訶薩

judge.reason: A correctly groups the epithets as the subject and translates "ཇི་སྙེད་པས" as "所有" (however many/all), fitting the Tibetan phrasing.

atts.t: 真實步入菩薩乘者應當如何安住、應當如何修行、應當如何降伏其心，我將為你解說。

i.sp: 真實步入
i.ev: Tibetan ཡང་དག་པར་བཞུགས་པ (Skt. samprasthita) uses ཡང་དག་པར 'correctly/properly', not 'truly/really'. 真實 reads as 'genuinely' (a claim about authenticity), whereas the Tibetan describes proper entry into the bodhisattva vehicle; english_academic has 'correctly entered'.
i.fx: 如理步入

atts.t: 如理步入菩薩乘者應當如何安住、應當如何修行、應當如何降伏其心，我將為你解說。

judge.reason: A translates "ཡང་དག་པར་" (samyak) accurately as "真實" (perfectly/truly), whereas B's "如理" usually corresponds to "ཚུལ་བཞིན་དུ་".

atts.t: 須菩提！於此真實步入菩薩乘者，應作是念：『無論多少眾生被攝於眾生之類中——或卵生，或胎生，或濕生，或化生，或有色，或無色，或有想，或無想，或非有想非無想，無論多少在眾生界中被假名施設為眾生者，我皆令彼等一切於蘊無餘涅槃界中般涅槃。』

i.sp: 真實步入
i.ev: Tibetan བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའི་ཐེག་པ་ལ་ཡང་དག་པར་ཞུགས་པ: ཡང་དག་པར is 'correctly/properly' (cf. Skt. samprasthita), not 'truly'; 真實 shifts the sense to authenticity. english_academic: 'correctly entered'.
i.fx: 如理步入

atts.t: 須菩提！於此如理步入菩薩乘者，應作是念：『無論多少眾生被攝於眾生之類中——或卵生，或胎生，或濕生，或化生，或有色，或無色，或有想，或無想，或非有想非無想，無論多少在眾生界中被假名施設為眾生者，我皆令彼等一切於蘊無餘涅槃界中般涅槃。』

judge.reason: A consistently and accurately translates "ཡང་དག་པར་" as "真實", aligning better with the Tibetan source than B's "如理".

atts.t: 世尊說：「須菩提，同樣地，菩薩不住於任何事物而行布施，其福德聚，須菩提，是因為不易衡量的緣故。」

i.sp: 其福德聚，須菩提，是因為不易衡量的緣故
i.ev: Tibetan ... བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་ནི། རབ་འབྱོར་ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ says the mass of merit is not easy to measure (the final ཕྱིར་རོ closes the 'why' answer; Skt. tasya puṇyaskandhasya na sukaraṃ pramāṇam udgrahītum has no 'because'). The Chinese 是因為...的緣故 leaves the merit mass with no predicate and reads as 'the merit mass is because it is hard to measure', which garbles the statement.
i.fx: 其福德聚，須菩提，不易衡量

atts.t: 世尊說：「須菩提，同樣地，菩薩不住於任何事物而行布施，其福德聚，須菩提，不易衡量。」

i.ev: Tibetan ends ...ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ (the final ཕྱིར་རོ marks a reason clause: "it is because ... not easy to measure"); english_academic renders "it is because". The translation ends with a bare statement 不易衡量 and drops the causal marker (Sanskrit has no explicit "because", so the loss is slight).
i.fx: ，須菩提，是因為其福德聚不易衡量

judge.reason: B faithfully translates "ཕྱིར་རོ།" with "是因為...的緣故" (because), whereas A completely omits the causal marker.

atts.t: 有多少無諸相具足，即有多少非虛妄，

i.sp: 有多少無諸相具足，即有多少非虛妄
i.ev: Tibetan 'ji tsam du mtshan phun sum tshogs pa med pa de tsam du mi brdzun te' is a correlative 'to whatever extent ... to that extent' (degree), per Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-23 ('ji tsam du ... bden par med pa de tsam ni mi brdzun'). The Chinese 有多少...有多少 reads as counting quantities of things, and 無諸相具足 is hard to parse.
i.fx: 在無諸相具足的程度上，即在同等程度上非虛妄，

atts.t: 在無諸相具足的程度上，即在同等程度上非虛妄，

judge.reason: B correctly interprets "ཇི་ཙམ་དུ་... དེ་ཙམ་དུ་..." as "extent/degree," which is much more precise here than A's countable "有多少".

atts.t: 「須菩提，在未來最後五百年，正法徹底壞滅之時，將會出現具足戒、具足功德、具足般若的菩薩摩訶薩。

i.sp: 具足戒、具足功德、具足般若
i.ev: Tibetan 'tshul khrims dang ldan pa, yon tan dang ldan pa, shes rab dang ldan pa' = 'possessing ethical discipline / qualities / wisdom' (Skt. guṇavantaḥ śīlavantaḥ prajñāvantaḥ). 具足戒 is the fixed Chinese term for full ordination vows (upasampadā), and 具足 also collides with the locked 諸相具足 (phun sum tshogs pa) in 6-7. The commentary (Chone 2-26) means the three trainings, not ordination.
i.fx: 具有戒、具有功德、具有般若

atts.t: 須菩提，在未來最後五百年，正法徹底壞滅之時，將會出現具有戒、具有功德、具有般若的菩薩摩訶薩。

judge.reason: A translates "ལྡན་པ" precisely as "具有" (possess) and avoids B's typographical error of an unmatched opening quote.

atts.t: 無眾生想，無壽者想，因為將不會生起人想。

i.sp: 無眾生想，無壽者想，因為將不會生起人想。
i.ev: Tibetan 'sems can du 'du shes pa ma yin | srog tu 'du shes pa ma yin | gang zag tu 'du shes 'jug par mi 'gyur ba'i phyir ro' is a single series; the closing 'phyir ro' answers the 'why?' of 6-19 for the whole series (self, sentient being, life-force, person). The Chinese 因為 attaches only to the last item, so it reads as if the person-perception explains the first two.
i.fx: 無眾生想，無壽者想，亦不會生起人想，故如此。

atts.t: 無眾生想，無壽者想，亦不會生起人想，故如此。

i.sp: 故如此
i.ev: Tibetan ends ...འཇུག་པར་མི་འགྱུར་བའི་ཕྱིར་རོ, i.e. the three non-perceptions are the stated reason ("because they have no perception of a sentient being ... "). 故如此 ("therefore it is so") is a vague, awkward rendering of ཕྱིར་རོ.
i.fx: 因為他們無眾生想，無壽者想，亦不會生起人想。

judge.reason: A accurately translates "ཕྱིར་རོ" as "因為" (because), whereas B uses "故如此" (therefore), which reverses the causal logic.

atts.t: 為什麼呢？因為諸聖人是以無為而區分的。

i.sp: 諸聖人
i.ev: Tibetan འཕགས་པའི་གང་ཟག་རྣམས is a locked term (འཕགས་པའི་གང་ཟག -> 聖者); the translation renders it 聖人 instead of the locked 聖者. Meaning is intact (cf. Vasubandhu 2-32, Chone 2-36).
i.fx: 諸聖者

atts.t: 為什麼呢？因為聖者眾人是以無為而有差別的。

i.sp: 聖者眾人
i.ev: Tibetan འཕགས་པའི་གང་ཟག་རྣམས་ (locked 聖者); རྣམས is only a plural marker. 眾人 ("the crowd of people") is an unneeded addition and also doubles 人/གང་ཟག.
i.fx: 聖者們

judge.reason: A correctly uses the locked term "聖者" for འཕགས་པའི་གང་ཟག, whereas B uses "聖人".

atts.t: 世尊說：須菩提，比起有善男子或善女人將此三千大千世界裝滿七寶並給予施物，若有人從此教法之法門中甚至僅受持四句偈，為他人解說並真實開示，從該基礎將產生更多、無數且無量的福德聚。

i.sp: 從此教法之法門中
i.ev: Tibetan ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གྲངས་འདི་ལས is the single locked term ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གྲངས -> 法門 ("this Dharma discourse/teaching"). The translation renders ཆོས་ separately as 教法 and then adds 法門, doubling the term (教法之法門).
i.fx: 從此法門中

atts.t: 世尊說：「須菩提，比起有善男子或善女人，將這三千大千世界以七寶完全充滿，作為施物而給予；若有人從這部教法之法門中，乃至僅僅受持四句偈，為他人解說並真實開示，他從這一基礎將產生更多無數、無量的福德聚。」

i.sp: 這部教法之法門中
i.ev: ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གྲངས་ ("Dharma discourse") is a single locked term rendered 法門; the translation splits it into 教法 + 法門, giving the redundant "教法之法門".
i.fx: 此法門中

judge.reason: A's "作為施物而給予" accurately conveys that the world filled with jewels is the object being given, unlike B's coordinate phrasing.

atts.t: 為什麼呢？須菩提，因為如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者諸佛的阿耨多羅三藐三菩提，是從此處出生的。

i.sp: 正等覺者諸佛
i.ev: Tibetan ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་རྣམས is one locked term (-> 正等覺者, plural); the translation renders སངས་རྒྱས་ twice (正等覺者 plus 諸佛), as if two items.
i.fx: 正等覺者們

i.sp: 因為如來
i.ev: Tibetan 6-47 has only དེ་ཅིའི་ཕྱིར་ཞེ་ན། ... འདི་ལས་བྱུང་སྟེ, ending in the continuative སྟེ; the causal ཕྱིར་རོ comes only in 6-48 (སྐྱེས་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ). The added 因為 in 6-47 creates a double "because" with 6-48 (cf. Kamalasila 3-78, which cites this clause as the reason).
i.fx: 如來

atts.t: 為什麼呢？須菩提，因為諸位如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者諸佛的阿耨多羅三藐三菩提，是從此處產生的；

i.sp: 正等覺者諸佛
i.ev: ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ (locked 正等覺者) already contains སངས་རྒྱས; the added 諸佛 renders it a second time as if a fourth epithet.
i.fx: 諸位如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者的阿耨多羅三藐三菩提

judge.reason: A's use of "產生" (arise/produce) is much more appropriate for bodhi (awakening) than B's "出生" (born).

atts.t: 世尊，如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者、佛指示我是住於無煩惱者之中最為第一，

i.sp: 正等覺者、佛
i.ev: The Tibetan has three epithets: de bzhin gshegs pa dgra bcom pa yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas. The glossary locks the whole compound yang dag par rdzogs pa'i sangs rgyas as 正等覺者; the sub-entry sangs rgyas = 佛 is already inside it. Rendering both makes a fourth epithet (佛) that the Tibetan does not have.
i.fx: 如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者

i.sp: 指示我是
i.ev: bstan (Skt. nirdiṣṭa) here means 'declared / designated' as foremost; 指示 in Chinese means 'to instruct or point out', which is a different act.
i.fx: 宣說我為

atts.t: 世尊，如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者諸佛宣說我是住於無煩惱者之中的第一；

i.sp: 正等覺者諸佛宣說我是
i.ev: The agent is singular: དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱིས (no རྣམས་; Skt sg.; 7-30 "དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས"). 諸佛 makes the declaring agent plural (all Buddhas) and doubles སངས་རྒྱས, already part of 正等覺者.

atts.t: 世尊，如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者將我宣說為住於無煩惱者之中的第一，

atts.t: 世尊，如果我這樣想：「我得到了阿羅漢位」，如來對我所謂的「善男子須菩提是住於無煩惱者之中的第一，

i.sp: 如來對我所謂的「善男子須菩提是住於無煩惱者之中的第一，
i.ev: Tibetan: de bzhin gshegs pas bdag la rigs kyi bu rab 'byor ni nyon mongs pa med par gnas pa rnams kyi mchog yin te = the Tathagata's act of declaring concerning me (Skt. na mam tathagato vyakarisyat ...). The Chinese turns the Tathagata's declaring into a noun phrase ('what the Tathagata so-called regarding me') and leaves an opened quotation that is closed only at the end of 7-31, so the 7-31 clause (which is Subhuti's own reason, lung mi ston lags so) falls inside the Tathagata's quoted words. The 'if I thought ...' clause is left with no verb for the Tathagata. Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-50 reads it as the Tathagata declaring conventionally that Subhuti is foremost of those abiding without affliction, while not declaring 'abiding' ultimately.

atts.t: 世尊，如果我這樣想：「我得到了阿羅漢位」，如來對我宣說：「善男子須菩提是住於無煩惱者之中的第一」，

i.sp: 如來對我宣說：「善男子須菩提是住於無煩惱者之中的第一」
i.ev: Sanskrit: sacen mama ... na māṃ tathāgato vyākariṣyad araṇāvihāriṇām agryaḥ ... ("if I thought ..., the Tathāgata would NOT have declared me ..."); the Tibetan verb is the negated ལུང་མི་སྟོན་ལགས་སོ in 7-31 (commentary bo-chone-drakpa-shedrub 2-50: "ལུང་ མི་སྟོན"). The translation supplies a positive main verb 宣說 after the "if I thought" clause, so the conditional reads "if I thought I had attained arhatship, the Tathāgata declares me foremost", the opposite of the sense; english_academic has "would not declare".
i.fx: 則如來不會對我宣說：「善男子須菩提是住於無煩惱者之中的第一」

atts.t: 世尊，如果我這樣想：「我得到了阿羅漢位」，則如來不會對我宣說：「善男子須菩提是住於無煩惱者之中的第一」，

judge.reason: A's phrasing is grammatically broken. B correctly supplies the necessary verb to make the split clause coherent in Chinese.

atts.t: 因為無所安住，故不授記為『住於無煩惱者』。」

i.sp: 故不授記為『住於無煩惱者』。」
i.ev: Tibetan ci la yang mi gnas pas na nyon mongs pa med par gnas pa zhes lung mi ston lags so: the honorific lags marks this as Subhuti speaking of the Tathagata, who does not declare. The Chinese has no subject for 不授記 and, because of the unclosed quotation in 7-30, the final 」 closes the Tathagata's supposed words, so the speaker is misassigned. English_academic supplies 'the Tathagata does not declare me'.

atts.t: 由於我無所安住，如來不授記我為「住於無煩惱者」。

atts.t: 須菩提回答說：「世尊，如來所宣說的法任何都不存在。」

i.sp: 如來所宣說的法任何都不存在
i.ev: Tibetan དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་གང་གསུངས་པའི་ཆོས་དེ་གང་ཡང་མ་མཆིས་ལགས་སོ = 'there is no dharma whatsoever that the Tathagata has spoken' (Sanskrit nāsti sa kaścid dharmo yas tathāgatena bhāṣitaḥ). The Chinese places 任何 after the noun as a floating quantifier ('the dharma spoken by the Tathagata, any, none exists'), which is awkward and could be misparsed; the scope of 'any' over dharma should be explicit.

atts.t: 須菩提回答說：「世尊，如來所宣說的任何法都不存在。」

judge.reason: A's "任何法都不存在" flows much more naturally in Chinese compared to B's awkward "法任何都不存在".

atts.t: 你認為應以那些大丈夫的三十二相來見如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者、佛嗎？

i.sp: 正等覺者、佛嗎
i.ev: Tibetan ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ is one epithet ('perfectly complete Buddha'; Skt samyaksaṃbuddha), so the series is Tathāgata, arhat, perfectly complete Buddha (three items). The enumeration '正等覺者、佛' makes 佛 a fourth separate epithet.

i.ev: Tibetan སངས་རྒྱས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་རྣམས་ནི་འདུ་ཤེས་ཐམས་ཅད་དང་བྲལ་བ is a plain predicate ('are free of all perceptions'), with no ཉིད; '即是' reads as an identity statement (Buddhas are freedom-from-perception), unlike 8-12/8-18 where དེ་ཉིད justifies 即是.

i.sp: 八十四萬億那由他諸佛
i.ev: Tibetan སངས་རྒྱས་བྱེ་བ་ཁྲག་ཁྲིག་འབུམ་ཕྲག་བརྒྱད་ཅུ་རྩ་བཞི (Skt caturaśīti-buddhakoṭi-niyuta-śatasahasrāṇi; Chone 2-98 and Kamalaśīla 3-162 repeat the same figure) is 84 x koti x niyuta x hundred-thousand; 「萬」 (ten thousand) does not render འབུམ་ཕྲག (hundred-thousand), so the figure is stated imprecisely.

atts.t: 須菩提！我令那些佛世尊歡喜且未曾令其心生厭離之所作，與後五百歲時，受取、書寫、受持、憶持、讀誦、完全通達此經者相比，須菩提！前一福德聚對於此福德聚，連百分之一也不及。

i.sp: 我令那些佛世尊歡喜且未曾令其心生厭離之所作，與後五百歲時，受取、書寫、受持、憶持、讀誦、完全通達此經者相比
i.ev: The Tibetan compares two masses of merit (བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་སྔ་མ vs བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་འདི་); Chone 2-98 spells it out: 'the merit of what I did ... and the merit of those who write this sūtra in the last five hundred'. The Chinese sets an act against persons (「所作」 vs 「者」) and leaves the comparison of merits implicit until the final clause.

atts.t: 須菩提！我令那些佛世尊歡喜而未令其心生厭離所作的福德，與後五百歲時受取、書寫、受持、憶持、讀誦、完全通達此經者的福德相比，須菩提！前一福德聚對於此福德聚，連百分之一也不及。

atts.t: 須菩提！若彼時有善男子或善女人將受持盡其所有之福德聚，若我宣說彼等善男子或善女人的福德聚，眾生將會發狂，且心神錯亂。

i.sp: 若彼時有善男子或善女人將受持盡其所有之福德聚，若我宣說
i.ev: The Tibetan is a single conditional: 'if I were to speak of the mass of merit of those sons/daughters of noble family who would fully uphold however great a mass of merit' (བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་ཇི་སྙེད་རབ་ཏུ་འཛིན་པར་འགྱུར་བའི ... དེ་དག་གི་བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་ངས་བརྗོད་ན). The translation splits it into two stacked 若-clauses, the first with no consequent, so it reads as 'if at that time there were such persons' and the logic is hard to parse; 'ཇི་སྙེད' is a relative modifier of the merit, not a separate condition.

atts.t: 再者，須菩提，此教法之法門不可思議，

i.sp: 此教法之法門

Rendering ཆོས་ with its separate locked value 教法 and then adding 之法門 doubles the term and produces a nonexistent genitive construction (cf. Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-100 ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གྲངས་འདི).

i.sp: 這部教法的法門
i.ev: ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གྲངས་ is a single locked compound (法門 = Skt. dharmaparyāya). Prefixing 教法 renders ཆོས་ a second time and reads as 'the Dharma-gate of the teaching'. Bo-vasubandhu 2-91 uses ཆོས་ཀྱི་རྣམ་གྲངས་འདི་ as one term.

judge.reason: Both translations accurately reflect the Tibetan source. The differences between '這部' / '此' and '是不可思議的' / '不可思議' are purely stylistic and equally valid.

atts.t: 須菩提！在此，正確趣入菩薩乘的人應該這樣想：『我要使一切眾生都在蘊無餘涅槃界中完全般涅槃。』

i.sp: 蘊無餘涅槃界
i.ev: The locked term for ཕུང་པོ་ལྷག་མ་མེད་པའི་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པ is 無餘涅槃 (the whole phrase 'nirvana without remainder of aggregates'); the translation prefixes a stray 蘊, giving 蘊無餘涅槃, which is not the locked term and parses oddly. The Tibetan is ཕུང་པོ་ལྷག་མ་མེད་པའི་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པའི་དབྱིངས (dbyings = 界).

atts.t: 須菩提！在此，正確趣入菩薩乘的人應該這樣想：『我要使一切眾生都在無餘涅槃界中般涅槃。』
須菩提！於此真實趣入菩薩乘者應作是念：『我當令一切眾生於蘊的無餘涅槃界中完全般涅槃。』

i.sp: 於蘊的無餘涅槃界中
i.ev: ཕུང་པོ་ལྷག་མ་མེད་པའི་མྱ་ངན་ལས་འདས་པའི་དབྱིངས་ is 'the realm of nirvāṇa without remainder of the aggregates'; the locked rendering 無餘涅槃 already contains the aggregates. Adding a separate '蘊的' is awkward and misparses the compound (Skt. anupadhiśeṣe nirvāṇadhātau).

judge.reason: A's traditional Buddhist phrasing ('於此真實趣入', '應作是念') is more stylistically fitting for a sutra translation than B's highly colloquial wording, while maintaining perfect fidelity.

atts.t: 你認為如來從如來燃燈佛處，有任何現等覺阿耨多羅三藐三菩提之正等菩提的法嗎？

i.sp: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提之正等菩提
i.ev: The Tibetan བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ is a single term, locked as 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提 (Skt. anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhi). Adding 之正等菩提 (the locked value of the sub-term ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ) renders the same words twice and creates an apposition the Tibetan does not have.

i.sp: 無上正等菩提——阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
i.ev: The Tibetan has one object, བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ (locked: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提). The translation renders it twice ('無上正等菩提' and '阿耨多羅三藐三菩提'), so it reads as two items or an inserted gloss; Sanskrit has the single anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim.
i.fx: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提

judge.reason: B awkwardly combines the locked term with a redundant repetition ('阿耨多羅三藐三菩提之正等菩提'). A handles the phrasing much more clearly without this redundancy.
