須菩提！既然並沒有任何法，能讓如來現等覺無上正等菩提——阿耨多羅三藐三菩提，

i.sp: 無上正等菩提——阿耨多羅三藐三菩提
i.ev: The Tibetan has one object, བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ (locked: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提). The translation renders it twice ('無上正等菩提' and '阿耨多羅三藐三菩提'), so it reads as two items or an inserted gloss; Sanskrit has the single anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim.
i.fx: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提

judge.reason: A again omits '無上', whereas B correctly includes it for 'བླ་ན་མེད་པ'.

atts.t: 復次，須菩提！若有任何人這樣說：『如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者，亦即是佛，現等覺了阿耨多羅三藐三菩提此無上正等菩提。』他就是在說不實之語。

i.sp: 亦即是佛
i.ev: The Tibetan list is དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས: Tathāgata, arhat, perfectly complete Buddha. 'ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས' is one epithet (locked 正等覺者, as rendered in 8-96 and 8-98); splitting off 亦即是佛 adds an equating clause absent from the Tibetan and is inconsistent with 8-96/8-98.
i.fx: 如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者

i.sp: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提此無上正等菩提
i.ev: The Tibetan བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ is one term (locked 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提); the added 此無上正等菩提 repeats it and adds a demonstrative 此 not in the Tibetan.
i.fx: 現等覺了阿耨多羅三藐三菩提

atts.t: 復次，須菩提！若有任何人這樣說：『如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者現等覺了阿耨多羅三藐三菩提。』他就是在說不實之語。
復次，須菩提！若有任何人作如是言：「如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者，現等覺阿耨多羅三藐三菩提之無上正等菩提而成佛。」彼即是妄語。

i.sp: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提之無上正等菩提
i.ev: The Tibetan has one object, བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ (locked: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提). The translation renders it twice ('無上正等菩提' and '阿耨多羅三藐三菩提'), so it reads as two items or an inserted gloss; Sanskrit has the single anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim.
i.fx: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提

i.sp: 而成佛
i.ev: The Tibetan ends མངོན་པར་རྫོགས་པར་སངས་རྒྱས་སོ, the verb already rendered 現等覺 (locked); there is no separate 'and became a Buddha' clause (Skt. abhisambuddhā). Bo-vasubandhu 2-101 has no such clause.
i.fx: （刪去「而成佛」）

judge.reason: A's classical phrasing ('妄語') is more idiomatic and suitable for this sutra context than B's modern phrasing ('不實之語').

atts.t: 為什麼呢？須菩提！因為如來現等覺阿耨多羅三藐三菩提此無上正等菩提之法，是完全不存在的。

i.sp: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提此無上正等菩提之法
i.ev: Tibetan has a single phrase བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་ (locked 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提) as the locus of awakening, with ཆོས་དེ་ ('that dharma') as the object of མངོན་པར་རྫོགས་པར་སངས་རྒྱས་པ. The translation renders the one phrase twice (transliteration plus an added gloss 此無上正等菩提) and makes 法 an appositive of the bodhi, so the dharma reads as the bodhi itself; Skt anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ with 'kaścid dharmaḥ' separate.
i.fx: 因為如來於阿耨多羅三藐三菩提中現等覺的任何法，皆不存在。

atts.t: 為什麼呢？須菩提！因為如來於阿耨多羅三藐三菩提中現等覺的任何法，皆不存在。

i.sp: 於阿耨多羅三藐三菩提中現等覺的任何法
i.ev: Tibetan བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ཏུ་མངོན་པར་རྫོགས་པར་སངས་རྒྱས་པའི་ཆོས is terminative (awakened to / as bodhi); Sanskrit 'anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim abhisaṃbuddhaḥ' takes bodhi as object. '於…中' reads as locative (a dharma realized 'within' bodhi) and is inconsistent with the rendering in 8-95/8-97/8-100.
i.fx: 如來現等覺阿耨多羅三藐三菩提的任何法，皆不存在

atts.t: 何以故？須菩提！因為如來現等覺阿耨多羅三藐三菩提、無上正等菩提之法，完全無所有故。

i.sp: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提、無上正等菩提之法
i.ev: The Tibetan has one object, བླ་ན་མེད་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་བྱང་ཆུབ་ (locked: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提). The translation renders it twice ('無上正等菩提' and '阿耨多羅三藐三菩提'), so it reads as two items or an inserted gloss; Sanskrit has the single anuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim.
i.fx: 阿耨多羅三藐三菩提之法

judge.reason: A's wording ('何以故... 無所有故') follows standard Buddhist syntax, matching the tone better than B's more colloquial style.

atts.t: 須菩提！任何菩薩若如是信解：『諸法無我，諸法無我』，如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者，佛即稱之為菩薩摩訶薩。

i.sp: 如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者，佛即稱之為
i.ev: Tibetan དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱིས is one agent (Skt tathāgatena arhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena); སངས་རྒྱས is the final noun of the epithet ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས (locked 正等覺者). The translation renders it as 正等覺者 and then adds 佛 as a separate subject, so the epithets read as four items; the added 佛 has no counterpart in the Tibetan.
i.fx: 如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者即稱之為

atts.t: 須菩提！任何菩薩若如是信解：『諸法無我，諸法無我』，如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者即稱之為菩薩摩訶薩。
須菩提！若有菩薩作如是信解：「諸法無我，諸法無我」，如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者、佛，即稱彼為菩薩摩訶薩。

i.sp: 正等覺者、佛
i.ev: The Tibetan epithet is དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས, three titles (Tathāgata, arhat, perfectly complete Buddha; Skt. tathāgatenārhatā samyaksaṃbuddhena). སངས་རྒྱས is part of the third title, already covered by 正等覺者; listing 佛 separately yields a fourth epithet (cf. 7-28 and 8-100, which use 正等覺者 alone).
i.fx: 如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者

judge.reason: B's '作如是信解' is slightly more standard, and keeping the Buddha's epithets together as a single list subject flows better.

atts.t: 你認為如來有般若慧眼嗎？

i.sp: 般若慧眼
i.ev: Locked rendering for ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་སྤྱན is 慧眼; the translation prefixes 般若 (the locked rendering of ཤེས་རབ alone), producing a non-locked, redundant compound.
i.fx: 慧眼

atts.t: 你認為如來有慧眼嗎？
汝意云何？如來有般若慧眼否？

i.sp: 般若慧眼
i.ev: ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་སྤྱན is the locked compound 慧眼; 般若 is the locked rendering of the bare word ཤེས་རབ and is not to be added in front of 慧眼, making a redundant doubled rendering.
i.fx: 慧眼

judge.reason: B translates the interrogative 'སྙམ་མམ' directly within the sentence ('你認為...嗎'), while A adds a separate phrase ('汝意云何').

atts.t: 如來有般若慧眼。

i.sp: 般若慧眼
i.ev: Tibetan ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་སྤྱན is one locked compound rendered 慧眼 ('eye of wisdom'). Prefixing 般若 renders ཤེས་རབ twice (般若 + 慧), duplicating the same element; the Sanskrit is only prajñā-cakṣus.
i.fx: 如來有慧眼。

atts.t: 如來有慧眼。
你認為如來有教法眼嗎？

i.sp: 教法眼
i.ev: Tibetan ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན (Skt dharma-cakṣus) has the locked rendering 法眼. The translation inserts 教法 (the locked rendering of the bare noun ཆོས), yielding 'eye of the teachings'. The commentaries take the Dharma eye as the eye for phenomena/the conventional: Kamalaśīla 3-184 'ཆོས་ཙམ་གྱི་ཡུལ་ལ་ནི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན' (the eye whose object is mere phenomena); Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-117 'ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན་གྱིས་ཀུན་རྫོབ་པའི་རབ་དབྱེ་ཐམས་ཅད' (all conventional distinctions). 'Teaching' is not the sense.
i.fx: 法眼

atts.t: 你認為如來有法眼嗎？
汝意云何？如來有教法之法眼否？

i.sp: 教法之法眼
i.ev: ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན is the locked compound 法眼. Adding 教法 (the locked rendering of bare ཆོས་) reads it as an eye of the doctrine or teaching. The commentaries define it differently: Kamalaśīla 3-184 'ཆོས་ཙམ་གྱི་ཡུལ་ལ་ནི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན' (the eye for the object that is mere phenomena); Vasubandhu 2-112 says it knows what is designated as dharmas and persons.
i.fx: 法眼

judge.reason: B correctly uses the locked term '法眼' for 'ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན', whereas A incorrectly changes it to '教法眼'.

atts.t: 如來有教法眼。

i.sp: 教法眼
i.ev: Tibetan ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན (Skt dharma-cakṣus) has the locked rendering 法眼. The translation inserts 教法 (the locked rendering of the bare noun ཆོས), yielding 'eye of the teachings'. The commentaries take the Dharma eye as the eye for phenomena/the conventional: Kamalaśīla 3-184 'ཆོས་ཙམ་གྱི་ཡུལ་ལ་ནི་ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན' (the eye whose object is mere phenomena); Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-117 'ཆོས་ཀྱི་སྤྱན་གྱིས་ཀུན་རྫོབ་པའི་རབ་དབྱེ་ཐམས་ཅད' (all conventional distinctions). 'Teaching' is not the sense.
i.fx: 法眼

atts.t: 如來有法眼。

judge.reason: B correctly strictly uses the locked term '法眼', whereas A incorrectly uses '教法眼'.

atts.t: 如果恆河的沙有多少，恆河也剛好變成有那麼多條，如果世間的世界變成如同那些沙數一般多，你認為那些世間的世界多嗎？

i.sp: 世間的世界
i.ev: Tibetan འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས (lokadhātu) is one locked compound rendered 世界. The translation splits it into འཇིག་རྟེན (世間) + ཁམས (世界), giving 'worlds of the world'.
i.fx: 世界

i.sp: 如果世間的世界變成如同那些沙數一般多
i.ev: Tibetan 'དེ་དག་གི་བྱེ་མ་དེ་སྙེད་ཀྱི་འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས' (Skt tāsu vā vālukāḥ, tāvantaś ca lokadhātavaḥ) says the worlds equal the grains of sand in those (many) Ganges rivers. The Chinese has no 'in those rivers', so 那些沙 can be read as the sand of the single original Ganges, which understates the number.
i.fx: 如果那些恆河中的沙粒有多少，世界也變成有那麼多

atts.t: 若恆河的沙有多少，恆河就有多少，若世界如同那些恆河的沙那麼多，你認為那些世界多嗎？

judge.reason: A correctly uses the locked term "世界" for འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས, whereas B redundantly uses "世間的世界".

atts.t: 那些世間的世界很多。

i.sp: 世間的世界
i.ev: འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས is locked as 世界; 世間 is the locked rendering of འཇིག་རྟེན alone and should not be added as a separate element.
i.fx: 那些世界很多。

atts.t: 那些世界很多。

judge.reason: B correctly applies the locked term "世界" for འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས, whereas A redundantly translates it as "世間的世界".

atts.t: 世尊言：「須菩提！在那些世間的世界中所有的眾生，他們各種不同意向的心流，我皆完全了知。」

i.sp: 世間的世界
i.ev: འཇིག་རྟེན་གྱི་ཁམས་དེ་དག is one locked compound, 世界; the translation renders it as 'worlds of the world'.
i.fx: 在那些世界中

atts.t: 世尊說：「須菩提，那些世界中有多少眾生，我完全了知他們種種不同意念的心流。」

judge.reason: A correctly uses the locked term "世界", while B redundantly translates the term as "世間的世界".

atts.t: 應以諸相具足見如來嗎？」

i.ev: Tibetan ends བལྟ་བར་བྱ་སྙམ་མམ ('do you think ... is to be seen?'); the verb སྙམ ('think') is not rendered, whereas 10-12 renders the parallel with 你認為. The question form in Sanskrit (द्रष्टव्यः ?) is kept, but the 'do you think' frame is lost.
i.fx: 你認為應以諸相具足見如來嗎？

atts.t: 你認為應以諸相具足見如來嗎？

judge.reason: B accurately translates སྙམ་མམ (do you think) as "你認為", which A completely omits.

atts.t: 因為如來所宣說的法，沒有任何存在的緣故。

i.sp: 沒有任何存在的緣故
i.ev: Tibetan དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་གང་བསྟན་པའི་ཆོས་དེ་གང་ཡང་མེད་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ: གང་ཡང་ ('any whatsoever') qualifies the dharma ('there is no dharma whatsoever that the Tathāgata taught'). In the Chinese, 任何 is attached to 存在, so the sense reads awkwardly as 'the dharma has no existence of any kind' and the 'no such dharma at all' sense is blurred.
i.fx: 因為如來所宣說的任何法，都不存在的緣故。

atts.t: 因為如來所宣說的任何法，都不存在的緣故。

judge.reason: A's "任何法，都不存在" is much more natural and precise in Chinese than B's "法，沒有任何存在".

atts.t: 須菩提！如果有人這麼說：『如來宣說了教法』，須菩提！他就是以執取不存在與顛倒在誹謗我。

i.sp: 以執取不存在與顛倒
i.ev: Tibetan མེད་པ་དང་ལོག་པར་ཟིན་པས; Sanskrit असतोद्गृहीतेन ('by what is wrongly grasped, the nonexistent'). Kamalaśīla (bo-kamalasila-tika 3-200) glosses ལོག་པར་འཛིན་པས as ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག་ཏུ་མངོན་པར་ཞེན་པས་ལོག་པར་ཟིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་དེ་མེད་: one act, a mistaken grasping of what does not exist. The Chinese 不存在與顛倒 reads as two separate items (grasping the nonexistent, and 'inversion').
i.fx: 以對不存在之物的顛倒執取而誹謗我

atts.t: 須菩提！如果有人這麼說：『如來宣說了教法』，須菩提！他就是以對不存在之物的顛倒執取而誹謗我。

judge.reason: B's phrasing "對不存在之物的顛倒執取" is much more natural and precise than A's literal but awkward "執取不存在與顛倒".

atts.t: 須菩提！所謂凡夫，如來說即非凡夫，

i.sp: 如來說即非凡夫
i.ev: Tibetan 'དེ་དག་སྐྱེ་བོ་མེད་པ་ཉིད་དུ་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་གསུངས་ཏེ' (Skt ajanā eva) says they are exactly 'non-beings' (skye bo med pa), playing on skye bo in so so'i skye bo; Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-134 glosses it as not established as skye bo in the ultimate sense. '非凡夫' can be read as 'not ordinary people (i.e. noble ones)', which the Tibetan does not say; the 'being' element of skye bo is lost.
i.fx: 如來說彼等即是無「生者」（非有情者）

atts.t: 須菩提！所謂凡夫，如來說彼等即是無生者，

i.sp: 無生者
i.ev: Tibetan སྐྱེ་བོ་མེད་པ་ཉིད (Skt. ajana) means 'non-persons / non-beings', i.e. no ordinary being is established as such. Kamalaśīla 3-222: དོན་དམ་པར་ནི་སྐྱེ་བོ་མེད་པ་ཉིད ('ultimately they are exactly non-beings'); Chone 2-134: དོན་དམ་པར་སྐྱེ་བོ་ཉིད་དུ་གྲུབ་པ་མེད་པར ('not established as beings ultimately'). 無生者 means 'those without arising/unborn' (無生 = anutpāda), a different concept, and does not convey 'no persons'.
i.fx: 如來說彼等即是非『生者』（勝義中並無眾生可得）

atts.t: 可以憑藉諸相具足來觀見如來嗎？

i.ev: Tibetan 'བལྟ་བར་བྱ་སྙམ་མམ' contains the verb 'think' (སྙམ, 'do you think ...'); the translation drops it and renders only 'can the Tathagata be seen by...'. Vasubandhu 2-131 quotes the same phrase with 'བལྟ་བར་བྱ་སྙམ་མམ'.
i.fx: 你認為可以憑藉諸相具足來觀見如來嗎？

atts.t: 你認為可以憑藉諸相具足來觀見如來嗎？

judge.reason: B correctly includes "你認為" to translate the Tibetan question marker སྙམ་མམ (do you think), which A omits.

atts.t: 世尊告言：「須菩提！固然應當攝受，但不應顛倒攝受，」

i.sp: 不應顛倒攝受
i.ev: Tibetan ལོག་པར་མི་བཟུང་ means 'one should not take hold wrongly/in a wrong way' (cf. Kamalaśīla 3-237: ལོག་པར་འཛིན་པ་ནི་ལམ་ལོག་པར་འཛིན་པ, grasping in a wrong way). 顛倒 is the standard rendering of ཕྱིན་ཅི་ལོག (viparyāsa), a different term, and adds a technical nuance; English academic has 'wrongly'.
i.fx: 不應錯誤地攝受

atts.t: 世尊告言：「須菩提！固然應當攝受，但不應錯誤地攝受，」

judge.reason: Both translations successfully convey the meaning of ལོག་པར་མི་བཟུང་ (should not take hold wrongly); "錯誤" and "顛倒" are both appropriate.

atts.t: 因此，稱之為如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者、佛。

i.sp: 正等覺者、佛
i.ev: The Tibetan ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས is a single epithet (perfectly complete Buddha), already fully rendered by the locked 正等覺者; appending a separate 佛 produces four epithets (如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者、佛) where the Tibetan has three (cf. Sanskrit tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha).
i.fx: 如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者

atts.t: 因此稱為如來、阿羅漢、正等覺者。

judge.reason: B correctly treats the locked term for 'perfectly complete Buddha' as a single entity without redundantly adding '佛' as A does.

atts.t: 名為聖《能斷金剛般若波羅蜜》的大乘經圓滿。

i.sp: 名為聖《能斷金剛般若波羅蜜》的大乘經
i.ev: Tibetan 'འཕགས་པ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་རྡོ་རྗེ་གཅོད་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ཐེག་པ་ཆེན་པོའི་མདོ' (Skt. ārya-vajracchedikā ... prajñāpāramitā): 'noble' (འཕགས་པ, locked 聖) qualifies the sūtra/title as a whole, but placing 聖 directly before the title in 名為聖《…》 makes it read as an odd, unattached word or part of the title.
i.fx: 名為《能斷金剛般若波羅蜜》的聖大乘經圓滿

atts.t: 名為《能斷金剛般若波羅蜜》的聖大乘經圓滿。

judge.reason: A properly places '聖' (noble) to modify '大乘經' (Mahāyāna sūtra), matching the reference and avoiding B's awkward placement before title marks.

atts.t: आर्य वज्रच्छेदिका प्रज्ञापारमिता यहाँ विद्यमान है।

i.ev: The Tibetan has ཞེས་བྱ་བ ("called/named") linking the title to the sūtra (Sanskrit has नाम); the Hindi gives the title with no "named/called", and uses Sanskrit title order rather than the Tibetan order (འཕགས་པ་ཤེས་རབ་ཀྱི་ཕ་རོལ་ཏུ་ཕྱིན་པ་རྡོ་རྗེ་གཅོད་པ་ཞེས་བྱ་བ). english_academic: "called the Diamond Cutter".
i.fx: आर्य प्रज्ञापारमिता, वज्रच्छेदिका नामक, यहाँ विद्यमान है।

atts.t: आर्य प्रज्ञापारमिता, वज्रच्छेदिका नामक, यहाँ विद्यमान है।

judge.reason: A correctly includes 'नामक' to translate the Tibetan 'ཞེས་བྱ་བ' (called), which B completely omits.

atts.t: भगवान श्रावस्ती में अनाथपिण्डद के जेतवन आराम में एक हज़ार दो सौ पचास भिक्षुओं के महान भिक्षु संघ और अत्यंत बहुत से बोधिसत्त्व महासत्त्वों के साथ विहार कर रहे थे।

i.sp: अत्यंत बहुत से बोधिसत्त्व महासत्त्वों
i.ev: Tibetan བྱང་ཆུབ་སེམས་དཔའ་སེམས་དཔའ་ཆེན་པོ་རབ་ཏུ་མང་པོ་དག = "very many bodhisattva mahāsattvas"; "अत्यंत बहुत से" is a clumsy double intensifier in Hindi.
i.fx: अत्यंत अनेक बोधिसत्त्व महासत्त्वों

atts.t: भगवान श्रावस्ती में अनाथपिण्डद के जेतवन आराम में एक हज़ार दो सौ पचास भिक्षुओं के महान भिक्षु संघ और अत्यंत अनेक बोधिसत्त्व महासत्त्वों के साथ विहार कर रहे थे।

judge.reason: Both translations accurately convey 'རབ་ཏུ་མང་པོ་དག་' (very many) with minor but acceptable stylistic variations.

atts.t: भगवान, तथागत, अर्हत्, सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध ने बोधिसत्त्व महासत्त्वों को जिस परम अनुग्रह से अनुगृहीत किया है, और तथागत ने बोधिसत्त्व महासत्त्वों को जिस परम परिन्दना से परिन्दित किया है, हे भगवान, यह आश्चर्य है! हे सुगत, यह आश्चर्य है!

i.sp: भगवान, तथागत, अर्हत्, सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध ने
i.ev: Tibetan: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ is the vocative addressed to the Buddha, while དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱིས is the agent (the Buddha as Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha); the Hindi comma list reads as four co-ordinate titles of one agent, with भगवान not marked as vocative (cf. english_academic "Blessed One, ... the Tathāgata, the arhat, the perfectly complete Buddha").
i.fx: हे भगवान, तथागत अर्हत् सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध ने

i.sp: परिन्दना से परिन्दित
i.ev: Tibetan ཡོངས་སུ་གཏད་པ means "to entrust"; Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-3 glosses it as the threefold entrusting (ཡོངས་སུ་གཏད་པ ... གནས་དང་ཆོས་དང་བཀར་གདགས་པ). "परिन्दना/परिन्दित" is an untranslated Sanskrit form (parīndanā) that conveys no meaning in Hindi.
i.fx: परम सौंपने (परिन्दना) से सौंपा है

atts.t: हे भगवान, तथागत अर्हत् सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध ने बोधिसत्त्व महासत्त्वों को जिस परम अनुग्रह से अनुगृहीत किया है, और तथागत ने बोधिसत्त्व महासत्त्वों को जिस परम सौंपने से सौंपा है, हे भगवान, यह आश्चर्य है! हे सुगत, यह आश्चर्य है!

i.sp: जिस परम सौंपने से सौंपा है
i.ev: Tibetan "ཡོངས་སུ་གཏད་པའི་དམ་པ་ཇི་སྙེད་པས་ཡོངས་སུ་གཏད་པ" = entrusted with how-great a supreme entrusting (Skt parīndanā). The Hindi uses the infinitive "सौंपने" as an abstract noun with instrumental, which is awkward and hard to parse; meaning is intact.
i.fx: जिस परम समर्पण (परीन्दना) से सौंपा है

judge.reason: A uses the proper Hindi term 'सौंपना' for 'ཡོངས་སུ་གཏད་པ' (entrust), whereas B uses 'परिन्दना', an obscure and non-standard loanword.

atts.t: तथागत ने बोधिसत्त्व महासत्त्वों को परम परिन्दना से परिन्दित किया है।

i.sp: परम परिन्दना से परिन्दित किया है
i.ev: Tibetan ཡོངས་སུ་གཏད་པའི་དམ་པས་ཡོངས་སུ་གཏད་དོ means "entrusted with the supreme entrustment" (english_academic); "परिन्दना/परिन्दित" is an opaque Sanskrit transliteration, not Hindi for "entrust".
i.fx: परम सौंपने (परिन्दना) से सौंपा है

atts.t: तथागत ने बोधिसत्त्व महासत्त्वों को परम सौंपने से सौंपा है।

i.sp: परम सौंपने से सौंपा है
i.ev: Tibetan "ཡོངས་སུ་གཏད་པའི་དམ་པས་ཡོངས་སུ་གཏད་དོ" = entrusted with the supreme entrusting (Skt parīndanayā parīndita). The infinitive "सौंपने" used as a noun is awkward Hindi; meaning intact.
i.fx: परम समर्पण (परीन्दना) से सौंपा है

judge.reason: A translates 'ཡོངས་སུ་གཏད་པ' using the natural and clear Hindi word 'सौंपना', avoiding B's obscure borrowing 'परिन्दना'.

atts.t: सुभूति, यहाँ बोधिसत्त्वयान में सम्यक् रूप से प्रविष्ट हुए को इस प्रकार विचार करना चाहिए: 'मेरे द्वारा जितने भी सत्त्व सत्त्व-संग्रह द्वारा संगृहीत हैं—चाहे वे अंडज हों, या जरायुज हों, या संस्वेदज हों, या औपपादुक हों, रूपी हों या अरूपी हों, संज्ञी हों, या असंज्ञी हों, या नैवसंज्ञी-नासंज्ञी हों, सत्त्व-धातु में प्रज्ञप्ति द्वारा जितने भी सत्त्व के रूप में प्रज्ञप्त हैं, उन सभी को मैं स्कन्ध-शेष-रहित निर्वाणधातु में परिनिर्वाण प्राप्त कराऊँगा।'

i.sp: मेरे द्वारा जितने भी सत्त्व सत्त्व-संग्रह द्वारा संगृहीत हैं
i.ev: Tibetan 'བདག་གིས་སེམས་ཅན་ཇི་ཙམ་སེམས་ཅན་དུ་བསྡུ་བས་བསྡུས་པ' and Sanskrit 'yāvantaḥ sattvāḥ sattvasaṃgraheṇa saṃgṛhītāḥ ... te ca mayā sarve ... parinirvāpayitavyāḥ' show the 'I' (བདག་གིས / mayā) as the agent of leading to nirvāṇa, not of the subsumption. Placing 'मेरे द्वारा' beside 'संगृहीत' makes it read as if the beings are subsumed by me.
i.fx: जितने भी सत्त्व सत्त्व-संग्रह द्वारा संगृहीत हैं ... उन सभी को मैं स्कन्ध-शेष-रहित निर्वाणधातु में परिनिर्वाण प्राप्त कराऊँगा

atts.t: सुभूति, यहाँ बोधिसत्त्वयान में सम्यक् रूप से प्रविष्ट हुए को इस प्रकार विचार करना चाहिए: 'जितने भी सत्त्व सत्त्व-संग्रह द्वारा संगृहीत हैं—चाहे वे अंडज हों, या जरायुज हों, या संस्वेदज हों, या औपपादुक हों, रूपी हों या अरूपी हों, संज्ञी हों, या असंज्ञी हों, या नैवसंज्ञी-नासंज्ञी हों, सत्त्व-धातु में प्रज्ञप्ति द्वारा जितने भी सत्त्व के रूप में प्रज्ञप्त हैं, उन सभी को मैं स्कन्ध-शेष-रहित निर्वाणधातु में परिनिर्वाण प्राप्त कराऊँगा।'

judge.reason: A correctly translates the Tibetan 'བདག་གིས་' (by me) as 'मेरे द्वारा', which B completely misses.

atts.t: हे सुभूति, क्योंकि जो बोधिसत्त्व अप्रतिष्ठित होकर दान देता है, हे सुभूति, उसकी पुण्यराशि का प्रमाण लेना सुकर नहीं है।

i.sp: प्रमाण लेना सुकर नहीं है
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པ' (Sanskrit 'pramāṇam udgrahītum') means to take the measure/extent. Hindi 'प्रमाण लेना' reads as 'take proof/evidence', which is a misleading collocation; 'माप करना' or 'परिमाण जानना' is the natural rendering. The same wording recurs in 5-2 and 5-4.
i.fx: उसकी पुण्यराशि का माप करना सरल नहीं है

atts.t: हे सुभूति, क्योंकि जो बोधिसत्त्व अप्रतिष्ठित होकर दान देता है, हे सुभूति, उसकी पुण्यराशि का माप करना सरल नहीं है।

judge.reason: B's 'प्रमाण लेना सुकर' is a more precise and standard academic translation for 'ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླ་བ་' than A's 'माप करना सरल'.

atts.t: हे सुभूति, तुम क्या सोचते हो? क्या पूर्व दिशा के आकाश का प्रमाण लेना सुकर है?

i.sp: प्रमाण लेना सुकर है
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླ' means to grasp the measure/extent of space; 'प्रमाण लेना' in Hindi suggests taking proof, not measuring.
i.fx: क्या पूर्व दिशा के आकाश का माप करना सरल है?

atts.t: हे सुभूति, तुम क्या सोचते हो? क्या पूर्व दिशा के आकाश का माप करना सरल है?

judge.reason: A's 'प्रमाण लेना सुकर' is a more precise and terminologically accurate translation for 'ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླ་བ་' than B's 'माप करना सरल'.

atts.t: भगवान ने कहा— हे सुभूति, उसी प्रकार दक्षिण, पश्चिम, उत्तर, ऊर्ध्व, नीचे की दिशा, विदिशाओं, और दशदिशाओं के आकाश का प्रमाण लेना क्या सुकर है?

i.sp: प्रमाण लेना क्या सुकर है
i.ev: Tibetan 'ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླའམ' means 'is it easy to measure'; 'प्रमाण लेना' reads as 'take proof' in Hindi.
i.fx: आकाश का माप करना क्या सरल है?

atts.t: भगवान ने कहा: हे सुभूति, उसी प्रकार दक्षिण, पश्चिम, उत्तर, ऊर्ध्व, नीचे की दिशा, विदिशाओं, और दशदिशाओं के आकाश का माप करना क्या सरल है?

judge.reason: A's 'प्रमाण लेना सुकर' more accurately reflects the precise terminology of 'ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླ་བ་' than B's 'माप करना सरल'.

atts.t: भगवान ने कहा: सुभूति, उसी प्रकार किसी में भी अप्रतिष्ठित होकर दान देने वाले बोधिसत्त्व की पुण्यराशि को, सुभूति, मापना सरल नहीं होने के कारण है।

i.sp: पुण्यराशि को, सुभूति, मापना सरल नहीं होने के कारण है
i.ev: Tibetan 'བསོད་ནམས་ཀྱི་ཕུང་པོ་ནི། རབ་འབྱོར་ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ' states a simple 'because ... is not easy to measure'. The Hindi construction 'पुण्यराशि को ... मापना ... के कारण है' is ungrammatical and hard to parse, and uses 'मापना' where 5-1 uses 'प्रमाण लेना' (inconsistent).
i.fx: उसकी पुण्यराशि का माप करना, सुभूति, सरल नहीं है; इसी कारण से।

atts.t: भगवान ने कहा: हे सुभूति, उसी प्रकार किसी में भी अप्रतिष्ठित होकर दान देने वाले बोधिसत्त्व की पुण्यराशि का माप करना, सुभूति, सरल नहीं है; इसी कारण से।

i.sp: सरल नहीं है; इसी कारण से।
i.ev: Tibetan ends "ཚད་གཟུང་བར་སླ་བ་མ་ཡིན་པའི་ཕྱིར་རོ" = "because ... is not easy to measure": the final ཕྱིར་རོ marks the non-measurability as the ground (cf. 5-1, same sentence, "क्योंकि"). The Hindi turns it into a trailing "इसी कारण से" (for this very reason), which makes the non-measurability a consequence of something prior and leaves the sentence dangling; the logical direction of the reason is changed/lost.
i.fx: भगवान ने कहा: हे सुभूति, उसी प्रकार, क्योंकि किसी में भी अप्रतिष्ठित होकर दान देने वाले बोधिसत्त्व की पुण्यराशि का माप करना, सुभूति, सरल नहीं है।

atts.t: इस प्रकार तथागत को लक्षण और निमित्त-रहित देखना चाहिए।

i.sp: लक्षण और निमित्त-रहित
i.ev: Tibetan མཚན་དང་མཚན་མ་མེད་པར་བལྟའོ is parsed by the commentaries as 'by marks, and as without signs/non-marks' (Kamalaśīla bo-kamalasila-tika 3-51: conventionally view the Tathāgata by marks, ultimately as markless; Vasubandhu 2-20: marks viewed as non-marks); Sanskrit lakṣaṇālakṣaṇataḥ. The Hindi 'लक्षण और निमित्त-रहित' can only be read as 'free of both marks and signs', which excludes the 'with marks / without signs' reading that the English cross-reference and Kamalaśīla give.
i.fx: लक्षण के रूप में तथा निमित्त-रहित (लक्षण-अलक्षण) रूप में देखना चाहिए

atts.t: इस प्रकार तथागत को लक्षण के रूप में तथा निमित्त-रहित देखना चाहिए।

i.sp: लक्षण के रूप में
i.ev: Tibetan "མཚན་དང་མཚན་མ་མེད་པར་བལྟའོ" = to be viewed with marks (མཚན) and without signs (མཚན་མ). Kamalaśīla (bo-kamalasila-tika 3-51): viewed by marks conventionally, without marks ultimately. "के रूप में" (as) says the Tathāgata is to be seen as a mark, not as possessing marks; the "with marks" sense is imprecise.
i.fx: लक्षणयुक्त तथा निमित्त-रहित

judge.reason: B correctly distinguishes 'having marks' and 'without signs', whereas A's phrasing implies 'without marks and without signs', which is inaccurate.

atts.t: ऐसा किसलिए है? हे सुभूति, क्योंकि उन बोधिसत्त्व महासत्त्वों में आत्मन् विषयक आत्म-संज्ञा प्रवृत्त नहीं होती,

i.sp: आत्मन् विषयक आत्म-संज्ञा
i.ev: Tibetan བདག་ཏུ་འདུ་ཤེས is the locked 'आत्म-संज्ञा'; the added gloss 'आत्मन् विषयक' is redundant and slightly awkward. Tibetan འཇུག་པར་མི་འགྱུར is also future/habitual ('will not engage'), while the next segment 6-20 switches to future.
i.fx: आत्म-संज्ञा प्रवृत्त नहीं होती

atts.t: ऐसा किसलिए है? हे सुभूति, क्योंकि उन बोधिसत्त्व महासत्त्वों में आत्म-संज्ञा प्रवृत्त नहीं होती,

judge.reason: B is more concise and directly matches the locked term 'आत्म-संज्ञा' without adding the redundant 'आत्मन् विषयक' seen in A.

atts.t: सत्त्व-संज्ञा नहीं होगी, जीव-संज्ञा नहीं होगी, और पुद्गल-संज्ञा में प्रवृत्त नहीं होंगे।

i.sp: सत्त्व-संज्ञा नहीं होगी, जीव-संज्ञा नहीं होगी, और पुद्गल-संज्ञा में प्रवृत्त नहीं होंगे
i.ev: Tibetan སེམས་ཅན་དུ་འདུ་ཤེས་པ་མ་ཡིན། སྲོག་ཏུ་འདུ་ཤེས་པ་མ་ཡིན། གང་ཟག་ཏུ་འདུ་ཤེས་འཇུག་པར་མི་འགྱུར is a parallel triad of the same construction (Sanskrit न सत्त्वसंज्ञा, न जीवसंज्ञा, न पुद्गलसंज्ञा प्रवर्तते). The Hindi changes the subject and verb in the third member (persons 'प्रवृत्त नहीं होंगे' versus the perceptions 'नहीं होगी') and the tense differs from 6-19; meaning intact.
i.fx: सत्त्व-संज्ञा प्रवृत्त नहीं होगी, जीव-संज्ञा प्रवृत्त नहीं होगी, और पुद्गल-संज्ञा भी प्रवृत्त नहीं होगी

atts.t: सत्त्व-संज्ञा प्रवृत्त नहीं होती, जीव-संज्ञा प्रवृत्त नहीं होती, और पुद्गल-संज्ञा भी प्रवृत्त नहीं होती।

judge.reason: A keeps 'संज्ञा' as the syntactic subject across all clauses, aligning better with the source phrasing than B's shift to an active subject.

atts.t: ऐसा किसलिए है? सुभूति, जिन्हें बुद्ध-गुण, बुद्ध-गुण कहा जाता है, तथागत ने कहा है कि वे बुद्ध-गुण नहीं हैं, इसीलिए;

i.sp: तथागत ने कहा है कि वे बुद्ध-गुण नहीं हैं
i.ev: Tibetan says སངས་རྒྱས་ཀྱི་ཆོས་དེ་དག་མེད་པར་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པའི་གསུངས་པ — the Tathāgata spoke of those buddha-qualities as non-existent (མེད་པར). Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-42 glosses it: དོན་དམ་པར་དེ་དག་མེད་པར་... ('ultimately those do not exist') and Vasubandhu 2-36 repeats བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས... མེད་པར. Hindi 'वे बुद्ध-गुण नहीं हैं' reads naturally as 'they are not buddha-qualities' (the Sanskrit abuddhadharmāḥ sense) rather than 'they do not exist'.
i.fx: तथागत ने उन बुद्ध-गुणों को अविद्यमान (अभाव रूप) कहा है

i.sp: इसीलिए;
i.ev: Tibetan ends the clause with ཕྱིར་ཏེ ('because'), answering དེ་ཅིའི་ཕྱིར་ཞེ་ན ('Why is that?'). Hindi closes with a dangling 'इसीलिए' ('therefore/for this reason'), which reverses the causal direction and is followed by another 'इसीलिए' in 6-50, so the reasoning is hard to parse.
i.fx: क्योंकि तथागत ने उन बुद्ध-गुणों को अविद्यमान कहा है;

atts.t: वह किसलिए? सुभूति, जिन्हें बुद्ध-गुण, बुद्ध-गुण कहा जाता है, क्योंकि तथागत ने उन बुद्ध-गुणों को अविद्यमान कहा है;

judge.reason: B correctly translates 'མེད་པར' (med par) as 'अविद्यमान' (non-existent), accurately reflecting the syntax and meaning of the Tibetan text.

atts.t: वह किसलिए? भगवान, यदि स्रोतापन्न ऐसा सोचे कि आत्मन् ने स्रोतापत्ति-फल प्राप्त कर लिया है, तो वह उसका आत्म-ग्राह ही होगा।

i.sp: आत्मन् ने स्रोतापत्ति-फल प्राप्त कर लिया है
i.ev: Tibetan "བདག་གིས་རྒྱུན་དུ་ཞུགས་པའི་འབྲས་བུ་ཐོབ་བོ་སྙམ་དུ" has བདག་གིས as the first-person pronoun 'by me' (Sanskrit "मया स्रोतआपत्तिफलं प्राप्तमिति"; english_academic: 'he had attained the fruit'). The locked term आत्मन् is for the doctrinal 'self' in བདག་ཏུ་འཛིན་པ, not for the pronoun. The Hindi makes 'the self' the agent who attained the fruit, which changes the sense of what the stream-enterer thinks.
i.fx: कि 'मैंने स्रोतापत्ति-फल प्राप्त कर लिया है'

atts.t: वह किसलिए? भगवान, यदि स्रोतापन्न ऐसा सोचे कि 'मैंने स्रोतापत्ति-फल प्राप्त कर लिया है', तो वह उसका आत्म-ग्राह ही होगा।

judge.reason: B correctly translates 'བདག་གིས' (bdag gis) as the first-person pronoun 'मैंने', whereas A incorrectly renders it as 'आत्मन् ने'.

atts.t: भगवान, यदि सकृदागामी ऐसा सोचे कि 'आत्मन् ने सकृदागामी-फल प्राप्त कर लिया है', तो वह उसका आत्म-ग्राह ही होगा।

i.sp: 'आत्मन् ने सकृदागामी-फल प्राप्त कर लिया है'
i.ev: Tibetan "བདག་གིས་ལན་ཅིག་ཕྱིར་འོང་བའི་འབྲས་བུ་ཐོབ་བོ་སྙམ་དུ": བདག་གིས is the pronoun 'by me' (cf. parallel 7-11 where the Hindi correctly has 'मैंने', and english_academic 'I have attained'). Rendering it as आत्मन् turns the thought into 'the self attained the fruit'.
i.fx: 'मैंने सकृदागामी-फल प्राप्त कर लिया है'

atts.t: भगवान, यदि सकृदागामी ऐसा सोचे कि 'मैंने सकृदागामी-फल प्राप्त कर लिया है', तो वह उसका आत्म-ग्राह ही होगा।

judge.reason: B correctly renders 'བདག་གིས' (bdag gis) as 'मैंने' (I), while A mistakenly treats it as the philosophical term 'आत्मन्' (Self).

atts.t: भगवान, यदि अर्हत् ऐसा सोचे कि 'मैंने अर्हत्त्व प्राप्त कर लिया है', तो वह उसका आत्मन् के प्रति ग्राह, आत्म-ग्राह ही होगा।

i.sp: आत्मन् के प्रति ग्राह, आत्म-ग्राह ही होगा
i.ev: Tibetan "དེ་ཉིད་དེའི་བདག་ཏུ་འཛིན་པར་འགྱུར" is one compound idea, 'that itself would be his self-grasping' (Sanskrit "स एव तस्यात्मग्राहो भवेत्"). The Hindi states it twice (a glossed 'ग्राह towards आत्मन्' plus the locked compound), which is redundant and awkward; 7-8 correctly gives only the compound.
i.fx: तो वह उसका आत्म-ग्राह ही होगा

atts.t: भगवान, यदि अर्हत् ऐसा सोचे कि 'मैंने अर्हत्त्व प्राप्त कर लिया है', तो वह उसका आत्म-ग्राह ही होगा।

judge.reason: A uses the locked term directly and elegantly. B adds an unnecessary, redundant explanatory phrase ('आत्मन् के प्रति ग्राह').

atts.t: भगवान, मुझे तथागत, अर्हत् और सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध बुद्ध ने क्लेश-रहित विहारी जनों में अग्र निर्दिष्ट किया है,

i.sp: तथागत, अर्हत् और सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध बुद्ध ने
i.ev: Tibetan "དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ་ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས" is three epithets of one person (Sanskrit "तथागतेनार्हता सम्यक्संबुद्धेन"). ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས is fully covered by सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध, so the extra 'बुद्ध' is redundant, and 'और' between the epithets can suggest separate persons.
i.fx: तथागत, अर्हत्, सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध ने

atts.t: भगवान, मुझे तथागत, अर्हत्, सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध ने क्लेश-रहित विहारी जनों में अग्र निर्दिष्ट किया है,

judge.reason: A correctly uses the locked term 'सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध' without redundancy. B unnecessarily adds 'बुद्ध' right after it, creating repetition.

atts.t: भगवान, यद्यपि मैं राग से रहित, वीतराग अर्हत् हूँ, तथापि भगवान, मैं ऐसा नहीं सोचता कि 'मैं अर्हत् हूँ'।

i.sp: राग से रहित, वीतराग अर्हत्
i.ev: Tibetan "འདོད་ཆགས་དང་བྲལ་བ་དགྲ་བཅོམ་པ" has a single phrase 'free from desire' (locked: འདོད་ཆགས་དང་བྲལ་བ = वीतराग; Sanskrit "अर्हन् वीतरागः"). The Hindi renders it twice ('राग से रहित' and 'वीतराग'), which is redundant.
i.fx: यद्यपि मैं वीतराग अर्हत् हूँ

atts.t: भगवान, यद्यपि मैं वीतराग अर्हत् हूँ, तथापि भगवान, मैं ऐसा नहीं सोचता कि 'मैं अर्हत् हूँ'।

judge.reason: Translation B redundantly translates the Tibetan for 'free from desire' twice by adding 'राग से रहित', whereas A correctly uses just the locked term 'वीतराग'.

atts.t: क्या तुम सोचते हो कि ऐसा कोई भी धर्म है जिसे तथागत ने तथागत, अर्हत्, सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध, बुद्ध दीपंकर से ग्रहण किया था?

i.sp: सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध, बुद्ध दीपंकर
i.ev: Tibetan has a single title 'ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་མར་མེ་མཛད' (perfectly complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara), where 'སངས་རྒྱས' is already the final element of samyaksaṃbuddha (Sanskrit: dīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya). Rendering both सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध and a separate बुद्ध duplicates 'Buddha', and the commas make the epithets read as separate persons.
i.fx: तथागत, अर्हत्, सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध दीपंकर से

atts.t: क्या तुम समझते हो कि ऐसा कोई भी धर्म है जिसे तथागत ने तथागत, अर्हत्, सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध दीपंकर से ग्रहण किया था?

judge.reason: The Tibetan phrase corresponds to the locked term 'सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध'. Translation A adds 'बुद्ध' separately, which is redundant.

atts.t: ऐसा कोई भी धर्म बिल्कुल भी नहीं है जिसे तथागत ने तथागत, अर्हत्, सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध, बुद्ध दीपंकर से ग्रहण किया हो।

i.sp: सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध, बुद्ध दीपंकर
i.ev: Tibetan has a single title 'ཡང་དག་པར་རྫོགས་པའི་སངས་རྒྱས་མར་མེ་མཛད' (perfectly complete Buddha Dīpaṃkara), where 'སངས་རྒྱས' is already the final element of samyaksaṃbuddha (Sanskrit: dīpaṃkarasya tathāgatasyārhataḥ samyaksaṃbuddhasya). Rendering both सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध and a separate बुद्ध duplicates 'Buddha', and the commas make the epithets read as separate persons.
i.fx: तथागत, अर्हत्, सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध दीपंकर से

atts.t: ऐसा कोई भी धर्म बिल्कुल भी नहीं है जिसे तथागत ने तथागत, अर्हत्, सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध दीपंकर से ग्रहण किया हो।

judge.reason: Translation B unnecessarily adds 'बुद्ध' after the locked term 'सम्यक्सम्बुद्ध', making it redundant, whereas A is concise and accurate.

i.ev: Tibetan ends ཡོད་སྙམ་མམ ('do you think there is...?'), with the verb of thinking (སྙམ) carrying the question; the Hindi drops 'do you think', and english_academic keeps it.

atts.t: क्या तुम समझते हो कि तथागत द्वारा कहा गया कोई भी धर्म है?

atts.t: त्रिसाहस्र-महासाहस्र लोकधातु में जितने भी पृथ्वी-रजकण हैं, क्या वे बहुत हैं?

i.ev: Tibetan ends མང་བ་ཡིན་སྙམ་མམ ('do you think they are many?'); the Hindi omits the verb of thinking (སྙམ), which english_academic retains.

atts.t: वह किसलिए? भगवान, इसलिए क्योंकि जो पृथ्वी-रजकण हैं, उन्हें तथागत ने रजकण नहीं कहा है।

i.sp: उन्हें तथागत ने रजकण नहीं कहा है
i.ev: Tibetan སའི་རྡུལ་གང་ལགས་པ་དེ་རྡུལ་མ་མཆིས་པར་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་གསུངས་པ: the Tathāgata taught it AS a non-particle (རྡུལ་མ་མཆིས་པར; Skt arajas tad bhāṣitam), a predication. The Hindi reads as 'the Tathāgata did not call them particles', a denial of the act of naming, which contradicts the next line (called 'particle'). Kamalaśīla 3-115 (རྡུལ་མེད་པ་ཁོ་ན) and Vasubandhu 2-54 confirm; compare 7-80 where the same structure is correctly rendered 'अधातु कहा है'.
i.fx: उन्हें तथागत ने रजकण-रहित (अ-रजकण) कहा है

atts.t: वह किसलिए? भगवान, इसलिए क्योंकि जो पृथ्वी-रजकण हैं, उन्हें तथागत ने अ-रजकण कहा है।

judge.reason: Translation B correctly uses the nominal negation 'अ-रजकण' matching the Tibetan 'rdul ma mchis par', rather than negating the verb like A does.

atts.t: ऐसा किसलिए है? भगवान, जो आत्मन् की संज्ञा, सत्त्व की संज्ञा, जीव की संज्ञा, और पुद्गल की संज्ञा है, वही सभी संज्ञाओं से रहित होने के कारण है।

i.sp: वही सभी संज्ञाओं से रहित होने के कारण है।
i.ev: Tibetan: 'གང་ལགས་པ་དེ་ཉིད་འདུ་ཤེས་ཐམས་ཅད་དང་བྲལ་བའི་སླད་དུའོ' (the answer to 'why?'; Sanskrit 'सैवासंज्ञा'). The Hindi makes the whole perception clause the subject of 'होने के कारण है' (that itself is because of being devoid), which is ungrammatical and obscures that the perception of self etc. is itself devoid of all perceptions (cf. Chone Drakpa Shedrub 2-76, 'འདུ་ཤེས་དག་དོན་དམ་པར་འདུ་ཤེས་སུ་གྲུབ་པ་དང་བྲལ་བ').
i.fx: वही सभी संज्ञाओं से रहित है।

atts.t: वह किसलिए? भगवान, इसलिए क्योंकि जो आत्मन् की संज्ञा, सत्त्व की संज्ञा, जीव की संज्ञा और पुद्गल की संज्ञा है, वही सभी संज्ञाओं से रहित है।

judge.reason: A provides a much more natural Hindi syntax using 'इसलिए क्योंकि' to translate the causal structure, whereas B is slightly awkward.

atts.t: वह किसलिए? क्योंकि बुद्ध भगवान सभी संज्ञाओं से रहित हैं।

i.sp: बुद्ध भगवान
i.ev: Tibetan 'སངས་རྒྱས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་རྣམས' has the plural marker 'རྣམས' (Sanskrit 'बुद्ध भगवन्तः', plural; Kamalaśīla 3-130 'སངས་རྒྱས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་རྣམས'). The Hindi 'बुद्ध भगवान' can be read as a single Buddha-Bhagavān, losing the plural (contrast 8-24 which uses the plural 'बुद्ध भगवानों').
i.fx: बुद्ध भगवान् (सभी बुद्धगण) सभी संज्ञाओं से रहित हैं

atts.t: वह किसलिए? क्योंकि सभी बुद्ध भगवान सभी संज्ञाओं से रहित हैं।

i.sp: सभी बुद्ध भगवान
i.ev: Tibetan སངས་རྒྱས་བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་རྣམས་ has only the plural marker རྣམས, 'the Buddhas, the Blessed Ones'; Sanskrit बुद्ध भगवन्तः likewise has no 'all'. 'सभी' before बुद्ध is not in the source (the 'all' belongs to perceptions only), and 'बुद्ध भगवान' reads as one apposition.
i.fx: बुद्ध भगवान

judge.reason: A correctly includes 'सभी' to translate the Tibetan plural marker 'རྣམས་' (rnams), whereas B omits it.

atts.t: और सुभूति, जो कुलपुत्र या कुलपुत्री इस प्रकार के सूत्र के इन शब्दों को ग्रहण करेंगे, धारण करेंगे, वाचन करेंगे, पढ़ेंगे, और पर्यवाप्त करेंगे, वे परिभूत होंगे,

i.sp: वे परिभूत होंगे
i.ev: Tibetan "མནར་བར་འགྱུར" means to be tormented/harassed. Kamalaśīla (3-160) glosses "མནར་བར་འགྱུར་ཞེས་བྱ་བ་ནི་སྤྱོ་བ་དང་། མཚང་འབྲུ་བ་ལ་སོགས་པས་གནོད་པར་བྱེད་པ" (harmed by abuse, insult etc.); Chone Drakpa Shedrub (2-97) lists illness, quarrels, beating and binding. The English academic has "tormented". Hindi "परिभूत" (despised/humiliated/overcome) narrows the sense to humiliation and is also obscure in Hindi.
i.fx: वे प्रताड़ित होंगे

i.sp: वाचन करेंगे, पढ़ेंगे
i.ev: The Tibetan lists five verbs: ལེན་པ (take up), འཛིན་པ (hold), འཆང་བ (keep/retain), ཀློག་པ (read), ཀུན་ཆུབ་པར་བྱེད་པ (master). The Hindi renders both འཆང་བ and ཀློག་པ as recitation/reading ("वाचन", "पढ़ना"), so the item "keep/retain" is lost (elsewhere in this batch འཆང་བ is "स्मरण रखे"/"पास रखेगा").
i.fx: ग्रहण करेंगे, धारण करेंगे, स्मरण रखेंगे, पढ़ेंगे, और पर्यवाप्त करेंगे

atts.t: वे अत्यन्त परिभूत होंगे।

i.sp: अत्यन्त परिभूत होंगे
i.ev: Tibetan "ཤིན་ཏུ་མནར་བར་འགྱུར" = severely tormented. Kamalaśīla (3-160) glosses the intensified "ཡོངས་སུ་མནར་བ" as harm by "གསད་པ་དང་བཅིང་བ" (killing, binding); Vasubandhu (2-88) speaks of "ཤིན་དུ་གདུང་བ" (intense suffering). "परिभूत" conveys humiliation/contempt, not severe torment.
i.fx: वे अत्यन्त प्रताड़ित होंगे

atts.t: वे अत्यन्त प्रताड़ित होंगे।

judge.reason: A accurately translates the Tibetan 'མནར་བ' as 'प्रताड़ित' (tormented), whereas B uses 'परिभूत' which means despised/disregarded.

atts.t: ऐसा क्यों? सुभूति, उन सत्त्वों द्वारा पूर्वजन्म में किए गए वे अकुशल कर्म जिनसे दुर्गति में जन्म होता, इसी जन्म में परिभूत होने के कारण, पूर्वजन्म में किए गए वे अकुशल कर्म जिनसे दुर्गति में जन्म होता, शुद्ध हो जाएँगे,

i.sp: इसी जन्म में परिभूत होने के कारण
i.ev: Tibetan "ཚེ་འདི་ཉིད་ལ་མནར་བས" = because tormented in this very life; Kamalaśīla (3-160) explains the torment as harm by abuse, killing and binding, and Chone Drakpa Shedrub (2-97) as illness, quarrels, beating and binding, whose suffering exhausts the past non-virtuous karma. "परिभूत" (humiliated/despised) misses this sense.

judge.reason: A consistently and accurately translates 'མནར་བ' (tormented) as 'प्रताड़ित', whereas B uses the inaccurate Sanskritism 'परिभूत'.

atts.t: किस प्रकार चित्त का निग्रह करना चाहिए?

i.sp: चित्त का निग्रह करना
i.ev: Tibetan སེམས་རབ་ཏུ་གཟུང་བར་བགྱི (Skt. cittaṃ pragrahītavyam) means 'fully hold/take up the mind' (cf. Kamalaśīla 3-167 སེམས་རབ་ཏུ་གཟུང་བར་བྱ་བ; 8-76 renders རབ་ཏུ་འཛིན་པ as भली-भाँति धारण). 'निग्रह' means restraint/suppression, a different nuance, and loses the རབ་ཏུ་ (pra-) 'fully' and གཟུང་ 'hold'.
i.fx: चित्त को भली-भाँति धारण करना चाहिए

atts.t: किस प्रकार चित्त को भली-भाँति धारण करना चाहिए?

judge.reason: B faithfully translates 'རབ་ཏུ་གཟུང་བ' as 'भली-भाँति धारण करना' (fully hold), whereas A's 'निग्रह करना' incorrectly implies restraining.

atts.t: ऐसा निवेदन किए जाने पर, भगवान् ने आयुष्मान् सुभूति से यह कहा:

i.sp: भगवान्
i.ev: Locked rendering for བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས is भगवान (used in 8-79, 8-80, 8-83, 8-91, 8-92); 8-93 uses the variant spelling with halant, inconsistent with the glossary.
i.fx: भगवान

atts.t: ऐसा निवेदन किए जाने पर, भगवान ने आयुष्मान् सुभूति से यह कहा:

judge.reason: A perfectly follows the locked term for the Blessed One as 'भगवान' without the halant, which B incorrectly adds.

atts.t: ऐसा किसलिए? सुभूति, जिसे 'चित्त-धारा, चित्त-धारा' कहा जाता है, तथागत ने उसे धारा-रहित कहा है।

i.sp: तथागत ने उसे धारा-रहित कहा है
i.ev: The Tibetan ends in the causal particle 'གསུངས་པའི་ཕྱིར་ཏེ' ('because the Tathāgata has taught it as no stream'), giving the reason answering 'དེ་ཅིའི་ཕྱིར་ཞེ་ན'; the Hindi drops the causal marker, so the clause reads as a bare statement rather than the stated reason (Skt. 'adhāraiṣā tathāgatena bhāṣitā' is likewise a reason clause).
i.fx: क्योंकि तथागत ने उसे धारा-रहित कहा है

atts.t: ऐसा किसलिए? सुभूति, जिसे 'चित्त-धारा, चित्त-धारा' कहा जाता है, क्योंकि तथागत ने उसे धारा-रहित कहा है।

judge.reason: B accurately captures the causal particle 'ཕྱིར་' (phyir) by including 'क्योंकि' (because), which A omits entirely.

atts.t: यदि कोई यह माने कि तथागत ऐसा विचार करते हैं कि 'मैंने धर्म का उपदेश दिया है', तो सुभूति, उसे इस प्रकार नहीं देखना चाहिए।

i.sp: यदि कोई यह माने कि
i.ev: The Tibetan conditional ("དགོངས་སོ་སྙམ་ན། རབ་འབྱོར་དེ་དེ་ལྟར་མི་ལྟ་སྟེ") is an address to Subhūti, who is told not to view it so; the Sanskrit makes it a question put to Subhūti. 'कोई' turns the address into a general statement about an unspecified person.
i.fx: यदि तुम ऐसा सोचो कि तथागत यह विचार करते हैं कि 'मैंने धर्म का उपदेश दिया है', तो सुभूति, तुम इसे इस प्रकार मत देखो।

atts.t: यदि तुम ऐसा सोचो कि तथागत यह विचार करते हैं कि 'मैंने धर्म का उपदेश दिया है', तो सुभूति, तुम इसे इस प्रकार मत देखो।

judge.reason: A correctly translates 'སྙམ་ན' (snyam na) in this context as 'यदि तुम ऐसा सोचो' (if you think), matching the 2nd person direct address.

atts.t: सुभूति, यदि कोई ऐसा कहे कि 'तथागत ने धर्म का उपदेश दिया है', तो सुभूति, वह असत् और मिथ्या ग्रहण करने के कारण मेरी निन्दा करेगा।

i.sp: मेरी निन्दा करेगा
i.ev: Tibetan "ང་ལ་སྐུར་བར་འགྱུར་རོ" (Skt abhyācakṣīta) means to slander or falsely accuse; Kamalaśīla 3-200 glosses "སྐུར་པ་ནི་དོན་མེད་པར་གླེང་བའི་ཕྱིར" (it is raising a baseless charge). 'निन्दा' means censure or criticism and does not convey the falseness of the charge.
i.fx: मुझ पर मिथ्या आरोप लगाएगा (मेरा अपवाद करेगा)

atts.t: सुभूति, यदि कोई ऐसा कहे कि 'तथागत ने धर्म का उपदेश दिया है', तो सुभूति, वह असत् और मिथ्या ग्रहण करने के कारण मुझ पर मिथ्या आरोप लगाएगा।

judge.reason: A's 'मिथ्या आरोप' is a more precise translation for 'སྐུར་བ' (bskur ba / slander / falsely accuse) than B's general 'निन्दा'.

atts.t: भगवान, क्या भविष्य में ऐसे कोई सत्त्व होंगे, जो धर्म के इस प्रकार के उपदेश को सुनकर दृढ़ श्रद्धा रखेंगे?
भगवान, क्या भविष्यत् काल में ऐसे कोई सत्त्व होंगे, जो इस प्रकार के धर्म-उपदेश को सुनकर दृढ़ श्रद्धा रखेंगे?

judge.reason: Both translations accurately capture the meaning of the Tibetan source and use the locked terms correctly.

atts.t: सुभूति, यदि तथागत द्वारा किसी भी सत्त्व को मुक्त किया जाता, तो वह ही तथागत द्वारा आत्मन् के रूप में आत्म-ग्राह होता।

i.sp: आत्मन् के रूप में आत्म-ग्राह
i.ev: Tibetan དེ་ཉིད་དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པས་བདག་ཏུ་འཛིན་པར་འགྱུར says only that this itself would be the Tathāgata's self-grasping (Sanskrit sa eva tathāgatasyātmagrāhaḥ). 'आत्मन् के रूप में' has no counterpart and, stacked on 'आत्म-ग्राह', is redundant and hard to parse (it can read as the Tathāgata being grasped as a self).
i.fx: तो वही तथागत का आत्म-ग्राह होता

atts.t: सुभूति, यदि तथागत द्वारा किसी भी सत्त्व को मुक्त किया जाता, तो वही तथागत का आत्म-ग्राह होता।

judge.reason: B redundantly adds 'आत्मन् के रूप में' alongside the locked term 'आत्म-ग्राह'. A is accurate and concise.

atts.t: सुभूति, जिसे आत्मन् का आत्म-ग्राह कहा जाता है, तथागत ने उसे ग्राह-रहित ही कहा है, फिर भी बाल-पृथग्जन इसे ग्रहण करते हैं।

i.sp: जिसे आत्मन् का आत्म-ग्राह कहा जाता है
i.ev: Tibetan བདག་ཏུ་འཛིན་ཅེས་བྱ་བ ('what is called grasping at a self'; Sanskrit ātmagrāha iti). 'आत्मन् का आत्म-ग्राह' doubles the self ('self's self-grasping') and does not parse as the Tibetan does.
i.fx: जिसे आत्म-ग्राह कहा जाता है

atts.t: सुभूति, जिसे आत्म-ग्राह कहा जाता है, तथागत ने उसे ग्राह-रहित ही कहा है, फिर भी बाल-पृथग्जन इसे ग्रहण करते हैं।

judge.reason: B redundantly adds 'आत्मन् का' before the locked term 'आत्म-ग्राह'. A correctly uses only the locked term.

atts.t: क्या लक्षणसम्पदा से तथागत को देखा जाना चाहिए?

i.ev: Tibetan ends བལྟ་བར་བྱ་སྙམ་མམ ('do you think ... is to be seen'); the Hindi renders a bare question and drops the 'do you think' (སྙམ་མམ), which 10-34 renders as 'क्या तुम सोचते हो'. english_academic keeps 'Do you think that'.
i.fx: क्या तुम सोचते हो कि लक्षणसम्पदा से तथागत को देखा जाना चाहिए?

atts.t: क्या तुम सोचते हो कि लक्षणसम्पदा से तथागत को देखा जाना चाहिए?

judge.reason: A correctly includes 'क्या तुम सोचते हो कि' to translate the interrogative 'སྙམ་མམ' (do you think?), which B completely omits.

atts.t: सुभूति, यदि कोई ऐसा कहे: तथागत ने आत्मन् विषयक आत्म-दृष्टि कही है,

i.sp: आत्मन् विषयक आत्म-दृष्टि
i.ev: Tibetan has only བདག་ཏུ་ལྟ་བར་གསུངས ('has spoken of the view of a self'); the locked rendering of བདག་ཏུ་ལྟ་བ is आत्म-दृष्टि, which already contains the self. The added 'आत्मन् विषयक' (concerning the self) is redundant padding not in the Tibetan.
i.fx: आत्म-दृष्टि

atts.t: सुभूति, यदि कोई ऐसा कहे: तथागत ने आत्म-दृष्टि कही है,

judge.reason: B redundantly adds 'आत्मन् विषयक' before the locked term 'आत्म-दृष्टि'. A correctly relies on the locked term alone.

atts.t: इस वज्रच्छेदिका-हृदय के सार का एक बार जाप करने से यह नौ करोड़ बार वज्रच्छेदिका का पाठ करने के समान हो जाता है।

i.sp: इस वज्रच्छेदिका-हृदय के सार का
i.ev: Tibetan རྡོ་རྗེ་གཅོད་པའི་སྙིང་པོ་འདི་ is a single term (locked: वज्रच्छेदिका-हृदय; སྙིང་པོ alone = सार). The translation applies both renderings to the one word སྙིང་པོ, yielding 'the essence of the Vajracchedikā-heart', which adds a second noun the Tibetan does not have (Chone Drakpa Shedrub 3-2 likewise has the single སྙིང་པོ). English: 'this essence of the Diamond Cutter'.
i.fx: इस वज्रच्छेदिका-हृदय का एक बार जाप करने से

atts.t: वज्रच्छेदिका के इस सार का एक बार जाप करने से यह वज्रच्छेदिका का नौ करोड़ बार पाठ करने के समान हो जाएगा।

i.sp: वज्रच्छेदिका के इस सार
i.ev: Tibetan རྡོ་རྗེ་གཅོད་པའི་སྙིང་པོ is a locked compound, to be rendered 'वज्रच्छेदिका-हृदय'; the translation instead splits it and uses the locked rendering of སྙིང་པོ alone ('सार'), so the longer locked term is not used.
i.fx: वज्रच्छेदिका-हृदय

judge.reason: A redundantly adds 'के सार' after 'वज्रच्छेदिका-हृदय', creating a double translation ('essence of the essence'). B avoids this redundancy.

atts.t: In the language of India: Diamond Cutter.

i.sp: Diamond Cutter
i.ev: Sanskrit title is Ārya Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Nāma Mahāyāna Sūtra (Noble Perfection of Wisdom called the Diamond Cutter, a Mahāyāna sūtra); children's text gives only the short name (locked term maps the whole title to Diamond Cutter).
i.fx: In the language of India: the noble perfect wisdom called the Diamond Cutter, a Great Vehicle sacred text.

atts.t: He finished eating his alms food. He put away his alms bowl and teaching robe. He washed his feet and sat cross-legged on his seat. He sat up straight with careful attention, ready to pay full attention.

i.sp: He finished eating his alms food.
i.ev: Academic: 'Having given up the alms of the later meal' - he set aside any further meal; children's text only says he finished eating.
i.fx: He did not take any more food. He put away his alms bowl and teaching robe.

i.sp: with careful attention, ready to pay full attention
i.ev: Tibetan/academic: 'having established mindfulness to the fore' (one phrase, locked 'pay full attention'); the text splits it into two and adds 'ready to'.
i.fx: He sat up straight and paid full attention.

atts.t: Subhuti, someone who has correctly entered the awakening hero's vehicle should think like this: 'I must help all kinds of living beings. This includes those born from eggs, or born from a womb. It includes those born from warmth and moisture, or miraculously born. It includes those having a shape, and those without form. It includes those having ideas, and those without ideas. It even includes those neither with ideas nor without ideas. However many exist in the realm of living beings, I will lead them all to complete freedom from sorrow in the expanse of freedom from sorrow with no group left over.'

i.sp: However many exist in the realm of living beings
i.ev: Academic: 'however many are designated by conceptual designation as sentient beings in the realm of sentient beings' - they are merely called/designated living beings; 'exist' asserts real existence and drops the designation point that sets up the paradox in 4-2.
i.fx: However many are called living beings in the realm of living beings, I will lead them all to complete freedom from sorrow in the expanse of freedom from sorrow with no group left over.

i.sp: I must help all kinds of living beings.
i.ev: Academic has the thought 'all those I shall lead to complete nirvana'; 'I must help' adds an obligation and a different action (help vs lead to freedom from sorrow).
i.fx: I will lead all living beings to freedom from sorrow. This includes...

atts.t: Subhuti, someone who has correctly entered the awakening hero's vehicle should think like this. 'I must help all kinds of living beings. This includes those born from eggs, and those born from a womb. It includes those born from warmth and moisture, and those miraculously born. It includes those having a shape, and those without form. It includes those having ideas, and those without ideas. It even includes those neither with ideas nor without ideas. However many are called living beings in the realm of living beings, I will lead them all to complete freedom from sorrow in the expanse of freedom from sorrow with no group left over.'

i.sp: I must help all kinds of living beings.
i.ev: The Tibetan/academic text has the bodhisattva resolve to lead all those beings to complete nirvana (complete freedom from sorrow); 'help' is vaguer and 'must' is not in the source (it says 'I shall lead').
i.fx: I will lead all kinds of living beings to freedom. This includes those born from eggs, and those born from a womb.

i.sp: It even includes those neither with ideas nor without ideas.
i.ev: The source simply lists this as the last category in the series; it has no 'even' emphasis.
i.fx: It includes those neither with ideas nor without ideas.

terms: neither with ideas nor without ideas
expanse of freedom from sorrow with no group left over

judge.reason: Translation A correctly includes "called living beings" (designated by conceptual designation), whereas B drops this meaning entirely.

atts.t: Why is that? Because whatever the Thus-Gone One taught as perfect marks are not perfect marks.

i.sp: whatever the Thus-Gone One taught as perfect marks are not perfect marks
i.ev: Academic: whatever the Tathagata has taught as the perfection of marks is itself no perfection of marks.
i.fx: Because what the Thus-Gone One calls perfect marks is not perfect marks.

atts.t: Subhuti, wherever there are perfect marks, there is falsehood.

i.sp: wherever there are perfect marks, there is falsehood
i.ev: Academic: to whatever extent there is the perfection of marks, to that extent there is falsehood (a matter of degree, not place).
i.fx: Subhuti, as far as there are perfect marks, that far there is falsehood.

atts.t: Wherever there are no perfect marks, there is no falsehood.

i.sp: Wherever there are no perfect marks, there is no falsehood
i.ev: Academic: to whatever extent there is no perfection of marks, to that extent there is no falsehood.
i.fx: As far as there are no perfect marks, that far there is no falsehood.

atts.t: Because of this, the Thus-Gone One said: 'Those who know this lesson on the teaching is like a raft should let go of even things, let alone what is not a thing.'

i.sp: Those who know this lesson on the teaching is like a raft
i.ev: Academic: Those who know this Dharma discourse to be like a raft should abandon even phenomena.
i.fx: Those who know that this lesson on the teaching is like a raft should let go of even things, let alone what is not a thing.

atts.t: "Why is that? Because noble persons are known by what is not made by causes."

i.sp: are known by what is not made by causes
i.ev: Academic: noble persons are 'distinguished by the unconditioned' (set apart by it), not merely 'known by' it.
i.fx: Because noble persons are set apart from others by what is not made by causes.

atts.t: That is why they are called a stream-enterer.

i.sp: they are called a stream-enterer
i.ev: Academic: 'he is called a stream-enterer' (singular); the children's text switches to plural 'they ... a stream-enterer', which is ungrammatical.
i.fx: That is why he is called a stream-enterer.

atts.t: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, you should listen closely.

i.sp: you should listen closely
i.ev: Academic translation: 'you should take an interest' (pay attention with interest/care), not just listening.
i.fx: Subhuti, you should pay close attention.

atts.t: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, imagine a man or woman gives away as many bodies as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River. Now imagine someone takes just a four-line verse from this lesson on the teaching and teaches it well to others. That person would create much more stored-up goodness from it. It would be too great to count or measure."

i.sp: That person would create much more stored-up goodness from it.
i.ev: The merit of teaching even a four-line verse is far greater than (bas) the merit of giving away bodies as numerous as the Ganges sand; the comparison is explicit.
i.fx: The person who teaches the verse would create much more stored-up goodness than the one who gave all those bodies. It would be too great to count or measure.

atts.t: Also, Subhuti, a man or woman might give away their bodies. They might give away as many bodies as there are sand grains in the Ganges River in the morning. They might do the same at midday and in the afternoon. Imagine they gave away their bodies like this for many millions of long ages.

i.sp: many millions of long ages
i.ev: Academic: 'many hundred-thousands of myriads of millions of eons' - a far larger, stacked number than 'many millions'.
i.fx: for countless long ages, many hundreds of thousands of millions of millions

atts.t: But what if someone hears this lesson on the teaching and does not give it up? They will create much more stored-up goodness than that. It is countless and cannot be measured. What need is there to even mention someone who writes it down, takes it up, keeps it, reads it, masters it, and teaches it to others?

i.sp: takes it up, keeps it, reads it, masters it, and teaches it to others
i.ev: Academic lists: writes it down, takes it up, holds it, keeps it, reads it, completely masters it, and extensively and correctly teaches it; 'holds it' and 'widely and truly' are dropped.
i.fx: writes it down, takes it up, holds it, keeps it, reads it, masters it completely, and teaches it to others widely and truly

atts.t: The Thus-Gone One spoke this lesson on the teaching for living beings who have rightly entered the best vehicle. He also spoke it for living beings who have rightly entered the best vehicle.

i.sp: the best vehicle. He also spoke it for living beings who have rightly entered the best vehicle
i.ev: Academic gives two different terms ('supreme vehicle' and 'foremost vehicle'); the children's text repeats the identical phrase, so the second clause reads as a mistaken repeat.
i.fx: for living beings who have rightly entered the best vehicle, and for living beings who have rightly entered the highest vehicle (note: glossary lists 'best vehicle' for both terms)

atts.t: Also, Subhuti, any place where this sacred text is taught will deserve respect. It will be honored by the world with its gods, humans, and jealous gods.

Also, Subhuti, think of any place where this sacred text is taught. That place will become worthy of respect. The world with its gods, people, and jealous gods will honor it. Every human, god, and jealous god will respect it.

i.sp: Every human, god, and jealous god will respect it.
i.ev: The source says once that the place becomes worthy of veneration by the world with its gods, humans and demigods; the final sentence repeats this and adds 'Every', which is not in the source.
i.fx: That place will become worthy of respect by the world with its gods, people, and jealous gods.

i.sp: The world with its gods, people, and jealous gods will honor it.
i.ev: The source says the place becomes worthy of (fit to receive) veneration; 'will honor it' states that they actually do so.
i.fx: That place will become worthy of being honored by the world with its gods, people, and jealous gods.

terms: world with its gods, people, and jealous gods

judge.reason: Translation B unnecessarily adds a repetitive sentence ("Every human, god, and jealous god will respect it") not found in the Tibetan source.

atts.t: If they hold an idea of a person, they are not called an awakening hero.

i.sp: If they hold an idea of a person
i.ev: 'even if they engage in a perception up to that of a person' - the sutra runs the list of ideas through to 'person'; 'even' and 'up to' are lost, and the 'because' link to the previous line.
i.fx: Even if they hold any of these ideas, right up to the idea of a person, they are not called an awakening hero.

atts.t: Why is that? Subhuti, there is no thing at all called 'truly entering the awakening hero's vehicle'.

i.sp: truly entering the awakening hero's vehicle
i.ev: 'having correctly entered the bodhisattva vehicle'; the same phrase is rendered 'correctly entered' in 8-80 and 8-84.
i.fx: there is no thing at all called 'correctly entering the awakening hero's vehicle'.

atts.t: Do you think the Thus-Gone One got any thing from the Thus-Gone One Dipankara to become fully awake to the highest, complete awakening?

i.sp: got any thing from the Thus-Gone One Dipankara to become fully awake
i.ev: 'any phenomenon by which the Tathagata fully awakened ... from Dipankara' - a thing by which he awakened, not a thing he received or got.
i.fx: Is there any thing by which the Thus-Gone One became fully awake to the highest, complete awakening in the time of the Thus-Gone One Dipankara?

atts.t: Blessed One, the Thus-Gone One did not get any thing at all from the Thus-Gone One Dipankara to become fully awake to the highest, complete awakening.

i.sp: did not get any thing at all from the Thus-Gone One Dipankara
i.ev: 'no phenomenon whatsoever by which the Tathagata fully awakened ... from Dipankara' - not a thing that was got.
i.fx: there is no thing at all by which the Thus-Gone One became fully awake to the highest, complete awakening in the time of the Thus-Gone One Dipankara.

atts.t: That is why the Thus-Gone One Dipankara foretold this to me: "Brahmin boy, in the future you will become the Thus-Gone One, the worthy one, the complete Buddha named Shakyamuni."
That is why the Thus-Gone One, Dipankara, foretold this to me. He said, 'Brahmin boy, in the future you will become a Thus-Gone One. You will be a worthy one, a complete Buddha named Shakyamuni.'

judge.reason: Translation A breaks the titles into two shorter sentences using indefinite articles, which is much more natural and readable for children than B.

atts.t: Subhuti, an awakening hero might firmly believe this: 'Things are without a self, things are without a self.' The Thus-Gone One, the worthy one, the complete Buddha calls that person a great awakening hero.

i.sp: an awakening hero might firmly believe this
i.ev: Says 'any bodhisattva who resolutely believes thus ... is called a great being' (a general statement about whoever believes), not a possibility.
i.fx: Subhuti, any awakening hero who firmly believes this: 'Things are without a self, things are without a self,' is called a great awakening hero by the Thus-Gone One, the worthy one, the complete Buddha.

atts.t: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, I fully know the streams of mind and the different thoughts of all the living beings in those world realms."

i.sp: the streams of mind and the different thoughts of all the living beings
i.ev: 'streams of mind of the diverse intentions of however many sentient beings'; intentions qualify the streams, not a separate item.
i.fx: I fully know the streams of mind, with all their different wishes, of every living being in those world realms.

atts.t: "Do you think the Thus-Gone One is seen by the full accomplishment of the form body?"

i.sp: is seen by the full accomplishment
i.ev: Tibetan/academic: 'is to be seen' (should be viewed) by the perfect accomplishment; the children's text loses the 'to be / should' sense.
i.fx: Do you think the Thus-Gone One should be seen by the full accomplishment of the form body?

atts.t: Subhuti, if anyone says, 'The Thus-Gone One has taught a teaching,' they would be lying about me. They would be holding onto a mistake about something that does not exist.

i.sp: They would be holding onto a mistake about something that does not exist.
i.ev: Academic: they slander me BY a mistaken grasping of what does not exist; the children's text splits this into two separate statements and loses the 'by' link.
i.fx: They would be lying about me, because they are wrongly holding onto something that does not exist.

atts.t: Why is that? Subhuti, as for what is called 'explaining the teaching', there is no teaching at all that you can hold onto as 'explaining the teaching'.

i.sp: you can hold onto
i.ev: Tibetan dmigs ('apprehended', locked children's rendering 'found'); 'hold onto' blurs it with the 'grasping' in 10-26.
i.fx: there is no teaching at all that you can find as 'explaining the teaching'.

atts.t: That highest, complete awakening is equal because it is without a self, without a living being, without a life, and without a person.

i.sp: is equal because it is without
i.ev: Academic: 'equal in being without a self...'; 'because' makes it a cause rather than the respect in which it is equal.
i.fx: That highest, complete awakening is equal in being without a self, without a living being, without a life, and without a person.

atts.t: Also, Subhuti, a son of a good family or a daughter of a good family might fill many world realms with the seven precious things. These realms are as numerous as the sand grains of the Ganges River. They might give them as a gift. But an awakening hero might gain patience in this lesson on the teaching being without a self and not born. From this, they make a pile of stored-up goodness that is vastly greater, countless, and beyond measure.

i.sp: From this, they make a pile of stored-up goodness that is vastly greater, countless, and beyond measure.
i.ev: The sutra compares the donor's gift with the bodhisattva's patience: the bodhisattva's merit is vastly greater than that of the one who gives the worlds full of precious things. The children's text only hints at this with 'But'.
i.fx: But an awakening hero might gain patience in this lesson on the teaching being without a self and not born. That hero makes a pile of stored-up goodness that is vastly greater than the gift, countless and beyond measure.

atts.t: Moreover, Subhuti, think of a son of a good family or a daughter of a good family. Suppose they ground all the earth in a world realm into powder. Imagine this world realm is a universe of a billion worlds. It would become like a bunch of tiny specks. What do you think, Subhuti? Would that bunch of tiny specks be very large?

i.sp: Would that bunch of tiny specks be very large?
i.ev: Tibetan mang ba / academic 'numerous': the question is whether the collection of specks is many, not large.
i.fx: Would that bunch of tiny specks be very many?

i.sp: ground all the earth in a world realm into powder. Imagine this world realm is a universe of a billion worlds.
i.ev: The earth particles are those in the whole universe of a billion worlds (three-thousandfold great thousandfold world system); calling it 'a world realm' and then redefining it is confusing.
i.fx: Suppose they ground all the earth in a whole universe of a billion worlds into powder.

atts.t: That bunch of tiny specks would be very large.

i.sp: very large
i.ev: Academic: the collection of subtle particles would be numerous (མང་བ = many), not large in size.
i.fx: That bunch of tiny specks would be very many.

atts.t: The Blessed One said, "Subhuti, anyone who has truly entered the awakening hero's vehicle should know, see, and understand all things in this way:"

i.sp: understand
i.ev: Academic: "know, see, and resolve upon" (མོས་པར་བྱ); "understand" repeats "know" and loses the third verb (trusting/resolving).
i.fx: should know, see, and have faith in all things in this way:

atts.t: Furthermore, Subhuti, think of a great awakening hero who fills countless world realms with the seven precious things and gives them all away as a gift. Now think of a son of a good family or a daughter of a good family. They might write down, learn, keep, read, understand, or fully teach others even just a four-line verse from this perfection, perfect wisdom. This person will create much more stored-up goodness. It will be too great to count or measure.

i.sp: think of a great awakening hero ... Now think of a son of a good family or a daughter of a good family. ... This person will create much more stored-up goodness.
i.ev: Academic: the merit of the one who writes/teaches even a four-line verse is "much more" than (compared to) the merit of the bodhisattva great being who fills world systems with the seven precious substances and gives them; the comparison between the two is the point.
i.fx: Furthermore, Subhuti, imagine a great awakening hero who fills countless world realms with the seven precious things and gives them all away as a gift. Now imagine a son or daughter of a good family who writes down, learns, keeps, reads, understands, or fully teaches others even just a four-line verse from this perfect wisdom. This person creates much more stored-up goodness than the hero did, too great to count or measure.

atts.t: Subhuti, think of a great awakening hero. They fill countless world realms with the seven precious things. They give them as a gift. Now think of a son of a good family or a daughter of a good family. They might write down, take up, keep, read, or master even just a four-line verse from this perfect wisdom. They might fully teach this perfection to others. Doing this creates much more stored-up goodness. It is countless and beyond measure.

i.sp: Doing this creates much more stored-up goodness.
i.ev: The segment is a comparison: the merit from filling countless world realms with the seven precious things and giving them is surpassed by the merit of the son or daughter of a good family who writes down, holds, reads, masters or teaches even a four-line verse ('compared to ... much more merit'). The children's text frames the two as separate scenes ('think of...') and never says the merit is more than the gift's, so the comparison is lost and 'Doing this' is unclear.
i.fx: Someone could fill countless world realms with the seven precious things and give them as a gift. But a son or daughter of a good family could write down, take up, keep, read, or master even one four-line verse from this perfect wisdom, or teach it fully to others. That person creates much more stored-up goodness than the gift, countless and beyond measure.

atts.t: Also, Subhuti, think of a great awakening hero, a great hero. They might fill countless world realms with the seven precious things and give them as a gift. Now think of a son of a good family or a daughter of a good family. They might write down, take up, keep, read, master, or fully teach to others even just a four-line verse from this perfect wisdom, this perfection. They will make much more stored-up goodness from that. It will be countless and cannot be measured.

i.sp: They will make much more stored-up goodness from that.
i.ev: The segment is a comparison: the verse-keeper produces much more merit than the bodhisattva who fills immeasurable world systems with the seven precious substances and gives them as a gift. The children's text presents two separate 'think of' scenes and never says the goodness is greater than that of the gift; 'from that' only points to the verse.
i.fx: They will make much more stored-up goodness than the hero who gave all those gifts. It will be countless and cannot be measured.

i.sp: this perfect wisdom, this perfection
i.ev: Tibetan shes rab kyi pha rol tu phyin pa is one locked term, 'perfect wisdom'; the extra 'this perfection' repeats it as if it were a second item.
i.fx: this perfect wisdom

atts.t: Also, Subhuti, think of a great awakening hero, a great hero. They might fill countless world realms with the seven precious things and give them as a gift. Now think of a son of a good family or a daughter of a good family. They might write down, take up, keep, read, master, or fully teach to others even just a four-line verse from this perfect wisdom, this perfection. They will make much more stored-up goodness than the hero who gave all those gifts. It will be countless and cannot be measured.

i.sp: this perfect wisdom, this perfection
i.ev: Tibetan/academic: 'this perfection of wisdom' (one term); the children's text splits it into two locked terms, which reads as two different things.
i.fx: this perfect wisdom (the perfection of wisdom)

judge.reason: Translation A correctly uses the locked glossary term "great awakening hero" once, whereas B redundantly adds "a great hero."

atts.t: The noble Great Vehicle sacred text called Perfect Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond is complete. This is the Diamond Cutter perfection of perfect wisdom.

i.sp: This is the Diamond Cutter perfection of perfect wisdom.
i.ev: Academic: a single title, "Diamond Cutter perfection of wisdom"; the added sentence repeats the title and "perfection of perfect wisdom" is redundant and confusing.
i.fx: The noble Great Vehicle sacred text called Perfect Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond (the Diamond Cutter) is complete.

terms: Perfect Wisdom that Cuts Like a Diamond

atts.t: 世尊在舍衛城的祇樹給孤獨園，也就是給孤獨的園林裡。他和一千二百五十名僧人，組成一個很大的出家人的團體。這裡還有極多的菩薩，也就是偉大的勇者，這些大菩薩都聚在一起。

i.sp: 他和一千二百五十名僧人，組成一個很大的出家人的團體
i.ev: The Tibetan/academic text says the Blessed One was gathered with a great community made up of 1,250 monks (the community consists of the monks), not that he and the monks together form the community.
i.fx: 世尊和一個很大的出家人的團體在一起，這個團體有一千二百五十名僧人。

atts.t: 那時候是清晨。世尊穿好下身的僧衣和僧衣，拿著乞食的缽。他走向大城市舍衛城，去尋求化緣的食物。

i.sp: 穿好下身的僧衣和僧衣
i.ev: Academic text: put on the lower robe and the outer robe; repeating '僧衣' twice with no contrast is confusing for children (locked terms are kept).
i.fx: 穿好下身的僧衣，再披上僧衣

atts.t: 「須菩提！真正踏上菩薩的車乘的人，應該這樣想：『不管有多少眾生算在眾生裡，不管是從蛋裡出生，從母胎出生，從溫濕處出生，還是神奇出生；不管是有形狀，還是沒有形體；不管是有想法的，還是沒有想法，或是非有想法也非無想法；不管在眾生的世界裡有多少被叫做眾生，我都要讓他們全都進入不剩組成部分的脫離憂苦境界，讓他們完全脫離憂苦。』」

i.sp: 不管有多少眾生算在眾生裡，不管是從蛋裡出生……我都要讓他們全都進入不剩組成部分的脫離憂苦境界，讓他們完全脫離憂苦。
i.ev: The academic text is one long enumeration; the children's version keeps it as a single very long sentence with stacked 'not matter' clauses, hard for ages 8-12 to follow.
i.fx: 分成短句，例如：『不管有多少眾生，不管是從蛋裡出生、從母胎出生、從溫濕處出生，還是神奇出生；不管是有形狀的還是沒有形體的；不管是有想法的、沒有想法的，還是非有想法也非無想法的——我都要讓他們全都進入不剩組成部分的脫離憂苦境界。』

terms: 不剩組成部分的脫離憂苦境界

atts.t: 「這是為什麼呢？因為這樣的人就不叫做菩薩了。」

i.sp: 因為這樣的人就不叫做菩薩了
i.ev: Academic text: 'because he is not called a bodhisattva'. '這樣的人...了' can be read as referring to the person who just had the thought of liberating beings, implying a consequence/reversal; the Tibetan only gives the bare reason, clarified in the next segment (one who holds a notion of being/life/person).
i.fx: 因為他不會被稱為菩薩。

atts.t: 只要沒有完美的特徵，就沒有虛假，

i.sp: 只要沒有完美的特徵，就沒有虛假
i.ev: The Tibetan/academic text is proportional: to the extent there is no perfect marks, to that same extent there is no falsity; '只要...就' turns it into a simple condition.
i.fx: 沒有多少完美的特徵，就有多少不虛假，

atts.t: 「須菩提，如果有人聽見別人講解這本經書，心裡生起一點點純淨的信任，如來全都知道他們。」

i.sp: 這本經書
i.ev: Source says 'such a sutra' (འདི་ལྟ་བུའི་མདོ་སྡེ, 這般經), a kind of sutra, not 'this book'.
i.fx: 這樣的經書

atts.t: 「須菩提，那些大菩薩也不會有「事物」的想法，更不會有「非事物」的想法，」

i.sp: 更不會有「非事物」的想法
i.ev: Source says they also do not form the notion of non-dharma; the two are parallel ('也'), not an escalation.
i.fx: 也不會有「非事物」的想法

atts.t: 即使有了事物沒有「我」的想法，這本身也會讓他們抓著「我」不放，

i.sp: 事物沒有「我」的想法
i.ev: Tangled for ages 8-12; 'notion of dharma-selflessness' is hard to parse in this word order.
i.fx: 即使有了「事物裡面沒有『我』」這樣的想法

atts.t: 所以，如來想要告訴我們：『明白這教導的一課就像木筏一樣，連事物都要放下，更何況是不是事物的東西呢。』

i.sp: 明白這教導的一課就像木筏一樣
i.ev: Academic: those who know this dharma teaching to be like a raft should abandon even dharmas; the child text makes 'understanding' the raft and drops the knowers as subject.
i.fx: 懂得這一課教導就像木筏的人，連事物都要放下，

i.sp: 更何況是不是事物的東西呢
i.ev: '是不是事物' reads as a yes/no question and is tangled for children.
i.fx: 更何況是那些不是事物的東西呢？

atts.t: 後來，世尊對尊敬的須菩提這樣說：

i.sp: 後來
i.ev: Source has 'moreover/further' (གཞན་ཡང་, 此外), not a later time.
i.fx: 接著

atts.t: 世尊，照我了解世尊說的意思，沒有任何事物是如來完全覺悟成最高、圓滿的覺悟的。

i.sp: 完全覺悟成最高、圓滿的覺悟的
i.ev: Stacked relative clause ending in '的的'; hard for children to parse.
i.fx: 如來完全覺悟到、而且是最高圓滿的覺悟的

atts.t: 為什麼呢？因為高尚的人，是靠不由原因造成來分別的。

i.sp: 是靠不由原因造成來分別的
i.ev: Academic: the noble ones are distinguished by the unconditioned; the phrase is awkward for ages 8-12.
i.fx: 因為高尚的人，是因為「不由原因造成」的東西而有不同的。

atts.t: 那位好人家的兒子或女兒，不管是好人家的兒子還是好人家的女兒，都會因為這樣得到一大堆福氣。

i.sp: 不管是好人家的兒子還是好人家的女兒
i.ev: Redundant repetition of 'son or daughter' makes the sentence clumsy; the segment only says that person produces much merit.
i.fx: 那位好人家的兒子或女兒，都會因為這樣得到一大堆福氣。

atts.t: 世尊說：「須菩提，如果有好人家的兒子或女兒，把七種珍寶裝滿十億個世界，當作禮物送給別人。不論是兒子還是好人家的女兒，送的禮物都非常大。可是，如果有人從這教導的一課裡，哪怕只記住一首四句的短詩，把這段詩句好好解釋給別人聽。這個人就會得到一大堆福氣，多得數也數不清，比送珍寶的人還要多！」

i.sp: 不論是兒子還是好人家的女兒，送的禮物都非常大。
i.ev: Academic/Tibetan contain no statement that the gift is very large; they only set up a comparison with the person who holds and explains a four-line verse.
i.fx: （刪去這句，直接接：）如果有人從這教導的一課裡，哪怕只記住一首四句的短詩，……

i.sp: 不論是兒子還是好人家的女兒
i.ev: Repetitive and tangled for children.

atts.t: 世尊說：「須菩提，如果有好人家的兒子或女兒，不管是好人家的兒子還是好人家的女兒，用七種珍寶裝滿十億個世界，把它們當作禮物送給人。另一方面，如果有人從這教導的一課裡，哪怕只記住一首四句的短詩，把這詩句為別人解說，清楚地教導別人。那麼，這個人會因此產生無法計算、無窮無盡的一大堆福氣，比前面那個人還要多。」

i.sp: 如果有好人家的兒子或女兒，不管是好人家的兒子還是好人家的女兒
i.ev: The Tibetan has one phrase, 'a son or daughter of good family'; the children's text repeats it redundantly, which is awkward for young readers.
i.fx: 如果有好人家的兒子或女兒，用七種珍寶裝滿十億個世界，把它們當作禮物送給人。

i.sp: 另一方面，如果有人從這教導的一課裡，哪怕只記住一首四句的短詩，把這詩句為別人解說，清楚地教導別人。那麼，這個人會因此產生
i.ev: The comparison (gift of worlds vs. holding and explaining one four-line verse) is correct but split into a long, tangled run of clauses.
i.fx: 另一方面，如果有人從這教導的一課裡，哪怕只記住一首四句的短詩，再講給別人聽，清楚地教導別人，這個人因此得到的福氣，會比前面那個人多得多。

judge.reason: A 無中生有地加入了「送的禮物都非常大」這句原文與學術翻譯皆無的內容，因此 B 在忠實度上較佳。

atts.t: 進入聖流的人會這樣想：「我得到了進入聖流的成果這個修行成果」嗎？

i.sp: 我得到了進入聖流的成果這個修行成果
i.ev: Academic: 'I have obtained the fruit of stream-entry'; the doubled 成果 / 修行成果 is clumsy.
i.fx: 進入聖流的人會這樣想：「我得到了進入聖流的成果」嗎？

atts.t: 為什麼呢？世尊，如果進入聖流的人心想：『我得到了進入聖流的成果。』把修行成果抓著不放，這本身就是抓著「我」不放了。

i.sp: 把修行成果抓著不放
i.ev: Academic: if the stream-enterer thinks 'I have attained the fruit', that itself is clinging to a self. Nothing says he clings to the fruit; the added clause shifts what is grasped.
i.fx: 為什麼呢？世尊，如果進入聖流的人心想：『我得到了進入聖流的成果。』這本身就是抓著「我」不放了。

atts.t: 為什麼呢？世尊，如果一個進入聖流的人心裡想：「我得到了進入聖流的成果。」把這當作自己的修行成果，這就表示他抓著「我」不放，也就是對自己抓著不放。

i.sp: 也就是對自己抓著不放
i.ev: The academic translation says only that this thought is itself his clinging to a self; the extra restatement adds nothing and blurs the point.
i.fx: 為什麼呢？世尊，如果一個進入聖流的人心裡想：「我得到了進入聖流的成果。」這就表示他抓著「我」不放。

judge.reason: B 精確譯出「這本身」（དེ་ཉིད），而 A 漏譯此詞，且在句末加上原文沒有的累贅解釋「也就是對自己抓著不放」。

atts.t: 只回來一次的人會心想：『我得到了只回來一次的成果』，覺得自己得到了這個修行成果嗎？

i.sp: 覺得自己得到了這個修行成果嗎
i.ev: Redundant restatement of the thought; academic has just 'would the once-returner think I have attained the fruit'.
i.fx: 只回來一次的人會心想：『我得到了只回來一次的成果』嗎？

atts.t: 世尊，如果只回來一次的人覺得有修行成果，這樣想：「我得到了只回來一次的成果。」那就是他抓著不放，抓著「我」不放，

i.sp: 覺得有修行成果，這樣想……那就是他抓著不放，抓著「我」不放
i.ev: Academic: if he thinks 'I attained the fruit', that is clinging to self; the extra 'has the fruit' and the vague 'clings' clause are tangled.
i.fx: 世尊，如果只回來一次的人這樣想：「我得到了只回來一次的成果。」那就是他抓著「我」不放，

atts.t: 不再回來的人會覺得自己有修行成果，而這樣想：「我得到了不再回來的成果」嗎？

i.sp: 會覺得自己有修行成果，而這樣想
i.ev: Redundant, tangled lead-in; academic simply asks whether he would think 'I attained the fruit'.
i.fx: 不再回來的人會這樣想：「我得到了不再回來的成果」嗎？

atts.t: 世尊，如來也就是值得敬重的修行者、圓滿的佛陀，說我遠離了困擾人的情緒，是心中沒有煩惱的人裡面最好的。

i.sp: 說我遠離了困擾人的情緒，是心中沒有煩惱的人裡面最好的
i.ev: Source only says the Tathagata declared me foremost among those dwelling without afflictions; the extra clause 'I am free of afflictions' is a duplicate not in the text.
i.fx: 世尊，如來、值得敬重的修行者、圓滿的佛陀，說我是心中沒有煩惱的人裡面最好的。

atts.t: 因為我的心不停留在任何地方，佛陀才沒有說我是個沒有困擾人的情緒、心中沒有煩惱的人。

i.sp: 佛陀才沒有說我是個沒有困擾人的情緒、心中沒有煩惱的人
i.ev: Academic: because I abide nowhere, the Tathagata does not prophesy me as 'one who dwells without afflictions'. The children's phrase is ungrammatical and tangled.
i.fx: 因為我的心不停留在任何地方，所以如來才沒有說我是「心中沒有煩惱的人」。

atts.t: 因此，這才被稱為佛的國土裡的佛國的佈置。

i.sp: 這才被稱為佛的國土裡的佛國的佈置
i.ev: Academic: therefore it is called 'buddha-field adornment'. The nested possessives are hard for children.
i.fx: 因此，這才被稱為「佛國的佈置」。

atts.t: 把它當作禮物，送給如來、值得敬重的修行者和圓滿的佛陀。跟這個比起來，如果有人從這教導的一課裡，哪怕只記住一首四句的短詩，並且真實清楚地說給別人聽，好好為別人說明。這個人因為這樣，會產生更多、數也數不清的福氣。」

i.sp: 如果有人從這教導的一課裡，哪怕只記住一首四句的短詩，並且真實清楚地說給別人聽，好好為別人說明。
i.ev: Academic: one long conditional sentence (hold even a four-line verse, explain and teach it to others); the children's rendering is a run-on with a redundant repeated clause.
i.fx: 如果有人從這一課裡，哪怕只記住一首四句的短詩，再清楚地說給別人聽，教給別人。

atts.t: 「還有，須菩提，如果在任何地方，有人讀出來或講述這教導的一課，哪怕只是一首四句的短詩，那個地方就會變成有天神、人和愛嫉妒的神的世間的佛塔。既然這樣，如果有誰能接受、寫下來、記在心裡、帶在身上、讀出來、完全明白，並且用心思考這教導的一課，那個人一定非常了不起，這就不用多說了。」

i.sp: 那個地方就會變成有天神、人和愛嫉妒的神的世間的佛塔
i.ev: Academic: that place becomes a stupa for the world with its gods, humans and asuras. The chain of 的 is tangled and hard for ages 8-12.
i.fx: 那個地方就會成為佛塔，受到有天神、人和愛嫉妒的神的世間所敬重。

terms: 有天神、人和嫉妒神的世間

atts.t: 你認為如來有說過任何事物嗎？」

i.sp: 如來有說過任何事物嗎
i.ev: Tibetan/academic: "Do you think there is any dharma taught by the Tathagata (that exists)?" The question is whether any taught thing exists; the children's text asks whether the Tathagata has spoken anything, which no longer matches Subhuti's answer that none exists and could suggest the Buddha taught nothing.
i.fx: 你認為有任何如來所說的事物存在嗎？」

atts.t: 你認為有任何如來所說的事物存在嗎？」

judge.reason: A 忠實保留了原文「如來所說的事物」作為主語以及「存在」（ཡོད）的句型結構，B 則改變了原本的句意結構。

atts.t: 「世尊，如來說了這麼多這教導的一課，真是太難得了！走得圓滿的人，真是太難得了！」

i.sp: 如來說了這麼多這教導的一課
i.ev: Academic: the Tathagata taught this teaching extensively; it is rare. "這麼多這教導的一課" is clumsy and suggests many different lessons.
i.fx: 「世尊，如來把這教導的一課說得這麼詳細，真是太難得了！走得圓滿的人，真是太難得了！」

atts.t: 「那是為什麼呢？世尊，因為所謂『我』的想法、『眾生』的想法、『生命』的想法和『人』的想法，其實就離開了所有的想法。」

i.sp: 其實就離開了所有的想法
i.ev: Academic: the so-called notions of self, being, life and person are themselves free of all notions; "就離開了" reads as if the notion departs.
i.fx: 其實它們本身就是遠離一切想法的。

atts.t: 「如果有眾生聽見這本經書，不驚慌、不害怕、也不恐懼，他們將會擁有最少見的特點。」

i.sp: 他們將會擁有最少見的特點
i.ev: Academic: such beings will possess supreme rarity/wonder (最極稀有), the same word rendered 難得 elsewhere; "特點" is an added, unclear notion.
i.fx: 他們是最難得的。

atts.t: 為什麼呢？須菩提！因為偏愛較低層次的人，沒有辦法聽懂這教導的一課。

i.sp: 沒有辦法聽懂
i.ev: Academic translation says such people cannot hear (聽聞) this teaching; the children's text shifts hearing to understanding.
i.fx: 因為偏愛較低層次的人，沒有辦法聽到這教導的一課。

atts.t: 還有，須菩提！任何好人家的兒子，或是好人家的女兒，當這些好人家的兒子或女兒接受、記住、讀誦，而且明白這類經書裡的句子時，他們將會受到折磨，

i.sp: 接受、記住、讀誦，而且明白
i.ev: Academic lists five verbs: take up, hold, remember, recite, fully understand; the children's text folds the first three into two verbs.
i.fx: 還有，須菩提！任何好人家的兒子或女兒，接受、守住、記住、讀誦，而且明白這類經書裡的句子，他們將會受到折磨，

atts.t: 為什麼呢？須菩提！那些眾生以前做過壞行為，本來會有不快樂的來生。因為這輩子受到折磨，他們以前做過、會帶來不快樂的來生的壞行為，就會被洗乾淨，

i.sp: 他們以前做過、會帶來不快樂的來生的壞行為
i.ev: Tangled nested clause for ages 8-12; meaning is intact (the earlier bad deeds that would lead to an unhappy rebirth will be purified).
i.fx: 因為這輩子受到折磨，他們以前做的那些壞行為就會被洗乾淨，不再帶來不快樂的來生，

atts.t: 須菩提！我記得在過去無數個漫長歲月之前，也就是在如來、值得敬重的修行者、圓滿的佛陀燃燈佛的更早以前，那時候出現過非常多位佛陀。我都讓他們很開心，

i.sp: 非常多位佛陀
i.ev: Tibetan/academic give a precise number: eighty-four hundred-thousand ten-millions (nayutas) of buddhas, and 'innumerable and even more innumerable' eons; the children's text reduces this to 'very many' and loses the 'even more innumerable' and 'even earlier' emphasis.
i.fx: 須菩提！我記得在很久很久、數也數不清的漫長歲月之前，在燃燈佛出現以前，更早更早的時候，出現過八十四億那由他百千位佛陀。我都讓他們很開心，

atts.t: 須菩提！我記得在很久很久、數也數不清的漫長歲月之前，在如來、值得敬重的修行者、圓滿的佛陀——燃燈佛出現以前，更早更早的時候，出現過八十四億那由他百千位佛陀。我都讓他們很開心，

i.sp: 數也數不清的漫長歲月
i.ev: Tibetan/academic: 'countless and even more countless' kalpas; the 'even more countless' intensification is lost.
i.fx: 在很久很久以前，數不清、而且比數不清還要更多更多的漫長歲月之前

i.sp: 八十四億那由他百千位佛陀
i.ev: The number 'eighty-four billion nayuta hundred-thousands' is kept as in the academic translation, but 那由他 is an unexplained hard word for ages 8-12.
i.fx: 八十四億那由他百千（多到難以想像的數目）位佛陀

judge.reason: A 忠實保留了原文中精確的數字「八十四億那由他百千」，而 B 卻將其簡化為「非常多位」，違反忠實度原則。

atts.t: 「須菩提！在那個時候，如果有哪個好人家的兒子或女兒，得到了這麼一大堆福氣。如果我把那些好人家的兒子，或是好人家的女兒，他們的一大堆福氣到底有多少都說出來，眾生聽了就會發瘋，心裡會亂成一團。」

i.sp: 如果有哪個好人家的兒子或女兒，得到了這麼一大堆福氣。如果我把
i.ev: The first sentence is an incomplete fragment; the Tibetan is one conditional sentence ('if I were to declare the merit of those who would hold so much merit').
i.fx: 須菩提！在那個時候，如果我把那些得到這麼一大堆福氣的好人家的兒子或女兒，他們的福氣有多少都說出來，眾生聽了就會發瘋，心裡會亂成一團。

atts.t: 因為只要有「人」的想法，他就不叫做菩薩。

i.sp: 因為只要有「人」的想法
i.ev: Academic: 'even if one gives rise to the notion up to (乃至) person' — a range running from being up to person; the children's text names only 'person' and loses the 'up to' range.
i.fx: 因為不管是把別人想成眾生，還是想成「人」，只要有這樣的想法，他就不叫做菩薩。
